section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: With MODE1.ALUSAT, fixed add/sub/neg/abs saturate to `0x7FFFFFFF` / `0x80000000`. The short compute forms (Type 2c), the multifunction ALU halves and the dual add/subtract may still wrap; this is unmeasured.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Open again (2026-11-16): whether reading an MR word into a register keeps the multiplier flags. The probe's `MRF = R1 * R2 (SSFR)` was assembled without the rounding modifier, so its MV flag proves nothing; the "float multiply with parallel add" item measured only a plain multiply (see CONFLICTS S10). {digikit-1116}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: The RECIPS/RSQRTS seeds come from two 128-entry tables, all measured; the low 15 mantissa bits are zero. Stock's divide helper uses RECIPS plus Newton steps, so the last bit of a division depends on the exact seed. Diagnostic reply publication ([finding 101](https://github.com/ElekLabs/digikit/blob/main/docs/findings/101-module-step-word-on-hardware.md)): the DSP's SPI2 is a slave and its transmit DMA walks two descriptors. Timing of the suspected overlap between DMA and diagnostic writes on silicon remains unmeasured. {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: On a real DT2 (OS 1.17), digikit's diagnostic word 25 arrived as 0 in 3,995 of 4,000 collected records. The old scheme delivered every second record in the emulator. `[hw]` {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Digikit's own `core/fx` and `core/dsp-voice` diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's reply word. Removing those clears restored delivery in the DN2 1.12 emulator; this does not identify stock firmware as the writer or establish silicon DMA timing. `[emu]` {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Keep hook diagnostics in a static word and copy it into the reply at the block tail, after all module calls. The revised design clears the static word rather than either reply record and passes the emulator regression; finding 101 says it had not yet run on a real DT2. A mark stored in the call that hangs the DSP cannot reach a tail that never runs, so the fault record retains the last completed block's mark. `[emu]` {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Three pieces of stock code: a vector stub, the wrapper `0x1c02a4`-`0x1c066b` (byte-identical on both images, 968 words, return label `0x1c04b7`; it calls the handler through the table at `0x2404b0` with `JUMP (M13, I12) (DB)` at `0x1c04b1`) and a return stub. SEC vector stub DT2 `0x1c0b7b` / DN2 `0x1c0acd`, generic stub `0x1c0b1e` / `0x1c0a70`, return stub `0x1c0be5` / `0x1c0b37`: the DN2 stubs sit `0xae` lower. `[doc]` (both images' bytes, two decoders)

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: What is saved: the stubs save R4, R8, R12, I6, I7, I12, B6, B7, PX and PCSTK; the wrapper saves the DAG, status, loop-stack and MR/MS registers and zeroes L0-L5 and L8-L15 for the handler. It picks its path by MODE1 bit 16 (RND32) of the interrupted code: with RND32 set it saves only R0-R2, R4 and S0-S15 and relies on the handler to keep the C callee-saved registers; with RND32 clear it saves R1-R15. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Never write these in module DSP code, not even with a save and restore: B7, L6, L7, M5, M6, M7, M13, IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT, FLAGS. The stock interrupt code may read them at any instruction, so an interrupt between the save and the restore sees the changed value. The wrapper needs a valid linear stack in I7 (L6 = L7 = 0) and M5 = 0, M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0. digikit's `sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md` generates one contract from this (classes clobber, keep, stack, never_write). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Finding 103 was partly withdrawn (2026-11-16): the old assembler mis-encoded several probe instructions, so the silicon run read MMASK as IMASKP, TPERIOD and TCOUNT as I0 and I1, LIRPTL (which SHARC+ lacks) as IMASK, and the cycle-counter reads of records 118-135 as LCNTR reads; it also dropped SSFR's rounding modifier and turned the dual multiply-plus-add into a plain multiply. The values listed in section 6 that came from these items are void; the non-cacheable ranges, REVID, IMASK, MODE2, the 59 value items and the block cycle counts stand (A41). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Calling convention: a delayed `CALL` with a frame; arguments in R4, R8, R12, more on the stack; result in R0. Most kernels come as a pair: `reset(record)` and `process(record, in, out, n)`, one 32-sample block per call. The prologue and epilogue cost ~20 instructions, about 0.6 per sample.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Every sample loop is a hardware `DO ... UNTIL LCE`. The loops are software-pipelined (the last stores come after the loop) and have a fast exit for n = 0 or 1.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Idioms worth copying: multiplier + ALU + data move in one instruction; post-modify DAG access with constant M6 = 1 and M5 = 0; RECIPS/RSQRTS seed plus Newton steps, using FAVG to halve; branch-free CLIP/ABS/MIN/MAX; FEXT to wrap an index; SIMD around copy loops; parameter ramps as "accumulator += step per sample"; MODE1 saved and restored around RND32 or SIMD.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Same code, different address: the shared kernels are byte-identical on DT2 and DN2 but sit at different addresses (biquad DT2 `0x1ccbd8`, DN2 `0xb81368`). Only the float divide `0x1c06ba` has one address on both. Calling a stock kernel therefore needs a per-device address row.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Hidden dependencies of stock kernels: The envelope reads a rate table at a device-specific absolute address. powf reads three tables and writes error words. Divide and rsqrt flip MODE1 bit 16 and restore it, so don't call them with SIMD or a loop active.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: The DSP sections are byte-identical between DT2 1.16 and 1.17 and between DN2 1.11 and 1.12 (digikit finding 53), so SHARC code and addresses carried over between those OS versions. `[doc]` {digikit-f53}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: digikit's recommendation: write your own kernels for the hot path; they can be faster (its estimate: interpolated delay 41 -> 15 instructions per sample, half-band 25 -> 10). Call stock only for the divide.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: The core runs at 1.000 GHz (DSP clock against the host's wall clock: 1000.1 MHz median). A block is 32 samples at 48 kHz = 666,667 cycles, 1,500 blocks/s. Earlier "~650k / ~975 MHz" figures were a unit error (counted in units of 1,024). Guards built on 650k are about 2.5 % too strict. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: On the Digitakt II, reply word 0 is a true load figure. It tracks an idle-task measure second by second, about 6.5k cycles/block below it (interrupts, RPC, timers outside the frame handler). This differs from the Digitone II, where dn2_firmware_explore found word 0 misreading. Add ~6.5k for the whole DSP. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: Device cycles are about 2x the emulator's instruction count for this project's own code, which reads samples from DDR. The emulator models no memory stalls. Stock render code is reported at ~9 cycles/instruction on the DN2. A hard stop that the emulator showed overshooting by ~25k overshot by ~75k on the unit. `[hw]` ([I36](../INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x))

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: Free budget with one plain stock track: about 330k cycles per block (calibration burn builds). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
text: Priorities 2-4 and 6 are unused, probably with configMAX_PRIORITIES = 7. A task at priority 2-4 runs only after Audio finishes its block and is preempted by the next one, so it cannot make Audio miss a block. Only work inside Audio, or at priority 6, can. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
text: Kernel globals: `pxReadyTasksLists` `0x2ca2e8` (20 bytes each), `pxCurrentTCB` `0x2ca3e0`, `uxCurrentNumberOfTasks` `0x2ca3e8`, `uxTopReadyPriority` `0x2ca3f0` (bit mask, `31 - leftz`), `xSchedulerRunning` `0x2ca3f4`, `uxSchedulerSuspended` `0x2ca414`. The TCB is 88 bytes and statically allocated (`xTaskCreateStatic` sw `0xb86014`). Stack overflow check method 2 (`0xa5a5a5a5`). No run-time stats are compiled in. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
text: `prvIdleTask` is at sw `0xb863ca` with no idle hook; its back edge is at sw `0xb863df`. `vTaskSwitchContext` sw `0xb85af7` stores `pxCurrentTCB` at sw `0xb85b6b`. Both are workable hook points for an idle counter or a task map, at ~250 device cycles per switch (~0.1 %). L2 code loads at byte `0x20000000` (sw `0xb80000`). "Audio" and "RPC" are created from internal-memory code (sw `0x1c3f6a`, `0x1c7775`). `[hw]` (hooks ran on the unit)

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: A late block is always a whole missed block. Audio is locked to the block interrupt. If one block's work runs past the next interrupt, that interrupt is lost and Audio runs one block later: an exactly one-block dropout, never drift. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: The stock engine governs its own per-block load. With 8 heavy stock tracks the Audio task ran at 99-100 % for whole 4 s windows and missed no block. Misses happen only when extra code inside the Audio task adds work the stock governor doesn't know about. So a custom engine must stop on a per-block deadline measured from the block start, with margin, not on an average budget. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: Provoked missed blocks (54 in one boot, three back to back) did NOT cause the sticky bitcrush. Neither did stock overload, nor sample loading at low load. The sticky "everything bitcrushed until reboot" appeared only with several custom-engine tracks at extreme settings. An emulator write audit showed no stray stores, so the cause is still open. Proven causes of a sticky whole-mix bitcrush from earlier builds: a render call much longer than a block with interrupts off; NaN/Inf reaching stock FX feedback; a value routed through a "free" stock parameter slot; overrunning the L2 area. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: Reading load by sampling word 0 (~17 reads/s = ~1 % of blocks) misses single late blocks. Count late blocks on the DSP side instead (task-switch gaps > 1.25 blocks). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
text: The SHARC writes two copies, at DM `0x266220` and `0x267220`. A selector at `0x261ca4` picks the copy being written (`0x266220 + (sel << 12)`), so write both. The ColdFire copies it every frame to `0x8000488C` (2,748 bytes, at most 687 words). The 16-bit halves arrive swapped. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
text: Word k is at `0x266220 + 4k`, not `+ k`. Two test builds wrote to the wrong place because of this; copy addresses from the compiler's disassembly. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
text: Which words are free (DT2 1.17, measured): 670-676 arrive untouched. heavylight's engine uses 672-676. Words 1-6 are rewritten by the firmware after the block, so writes there never arrive. Word 5 is the firmware's while a track plays (unlike the DN2). 677-686 are the firmware's. From word 7 on there is a per-track table: 21 words per track at `0x8000488C + 0x1C + 84*track`. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Render `FUN_1c5576 -> FUN_1c5615`, only caller `FUN_1c642a` (selector 2). Replace the body. Do not patch the call at `0x1c6af1`. The stock renderer costs ~1,720 instructions per 32-sample call. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Call: R4 = voice record (`0x2412cc + v*0x1d8`, 32 records), R8 = output (32 floats, 48 kHz, int16/32768 scale), R12 = 32. Voices are rendered in ascending order 0..31, so a new block starts when v <= last v. Record words: w00 sample pointer (int16 mono, L = voice 2t, R = 2t+1), w62/63 length, w64/65 loop start, w68/69 end (Q31), w6a/6b step (Q31, 96 kHz units), w6c/6d phase, bytes 0x1b8 active / 0x1b9 stop / 0x1bb reverse / 0x1bc loop, w72 = a (tempo fit, float) and w73 = b (pitch ratio). A trigger is visible as w70 == w71 == 0. +4 is a 96 kHz work buffer and +0x104 is decimator state, not scratch. Tempo is a float BPM at DM `0x252d50`. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Stock STRETCH: fixed 2,048-sample grains, 128-sample crossfade, linear interpolation. `a = BPM*(end-start)/(96000*120*2^bars)`, grid speed `clamp(a, 0.125, 4) + P - b`. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Knob frame working copy: short at `0x2558dc + 0xde + 0x60*track` (the hidden CFADE slot, 0..0x7f00). Routing a value through this "free" slot also feeds a stock per-voice flag that acts on the delay feedback (`FUN_1c24e9`, slot struct `0x2506ec + v*0xdc + 0x10`). That leaked into the delay and once caused a sticky bitcrush. Check every reused slot with a memory-write diff of the stock chain. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: The SHARC upload in MAIN OS checks only `length <= 1 MiB` (no fixed size). Insert new boot blocks before FINAL. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
text: Samples go to the DSP over link port 0 (LP0_CTL `0x30FFE000`; SEC sources 81/82/168), not over the frame link. LP1 is unused. One transfer is 0x401 words: a tag and 1,024 payload words. Tag `0xFFFFFFFF` means a slot header: slot, startL, startR, rate, len. Stereo means startL != startR. A tag below `0x19200` is a page number into the 400 MiB DDR sample pool at `0x8422B9C8`. This is the RPC-task work the owner saw while samples load.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
text: Slot table: 0x14-byte records at DM `0x257810 + slot*0x14` (start L/R relative to the pool, length, ...), at most 0x401 slots.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
text: Track t owns voices 2t and 2t+1, with no dynamic allocation (unlike the DN2). The frame's trig mask is at payload `0x22` (bit t = track t). `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: L2: the static analysis says `0x2001ab7c..0x20100000` minus `0x200fa000..0x200fe000` is free, but going past `0x200f5a74` gave clicks and leaks into the delay on the unit. Keep your data at or below that. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: External DDR: the stock output buffer (`0x8045b3c0`) and the sample data are in DDR. Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit (continuous tone), although the emulator was bit-identical. Render into L2 and copy once per block. Read int16 samples two at a time. `[hw]` ([I17](../INCIDENTS.md#i17-per-sample-stores-to-the-ddr-output-buffer-crashed-the-unit))

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: DM and PM data caches are not coherent on DDR (DN2 finding). Don't write through one bus and read through the other. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: Keep long calls short with interrupts off: a watchdog of at most ~1M cycles per call. Burns of ~1.27M with interrupts off left no lasting harm; longer calls knocked the audio stream out of step for good. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: Save MODE1 on entry and restore it on exit. A changed MODE1 alters the whole stock DSP until reboot. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: Never let NaN/Inf/huge values leave the machine: per-sample guard `!(|x| < 1e6)` -> 0 and restart the voice, clip to ±2. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: `double` is 32-bit float. A read position in float loses resolution from ~22 s into a sample, which sounds like sample-rate reduction. Use Q32.32 fixed point for positions. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: No integer `/` or `%` where the operand can be 0 (`___umod32` runs LCNTR = 32 - leftz(x); 0 means a hang).

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: No loops with early exit (`break`/`return`): they become DO loops left by a jump.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: `int more = a < b; while (more)` compiled into an endless loop. Write a counted `for` with an `if` body.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: Large initialised `static const float` tables arrive as garbage, so compute them at run time. Complex float expressions passed as arguments lost terms. `static int a = 1, b;` lost `b`. Keep compound conditions simple. Pass at most 3 arguments (stack arguments are passed wrongly) or a struct pointer.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: selas: multifunction (MUL+ALU) and dual-load forms are encoded wrongly; `Ia = MODIFY(Ib, ..)` becomes `Ib = ..`; system registers (MODE1, LCNTR, EMUCLK) moved in 48-bit form are wrong, so use compressed code. Negative shift immediates are wrong (`023e 0000` vs stock `023e 7800`: ILOPI on the unit). Shift by a register.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: selcc treats R3, R5-R7 as scratch where the ADI ABI preserves them: save them at the bridge.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: A selcc peephole bug (frame-reload forwarding clobbering the reload register) was patched locally. The patch also added a `SELCC_SAFE=1` switch that skips the post-allocation peepholes. If code misbehaves only when optimised, try that.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: DAG registers moved via the same DAG's addressing hang the unit; move them through R registers. Same rule as the DN2 skill.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Read-only USB SysEx probe in MAIN OS (heavylight's dt2-keyframer, derived from irpina/digihealth via dn2_firmware_explore): `F0 00 20 3C 7D 00 <pack7> F7`. Commands: HELLO 1 (returns word 0) and PEEK 3 (address, up to 256 bytes). There is no write command. It hooks the SysEx router at `0x40120006` (router `0x4011ffda`, header `0x4021e5d2`, send `0x40121d2a`, USB port 2), and the router itself drops device id 0x7D. It fits in 532 bytes of a free 896-byte run in MAIN OS 1.17 (`0x402e4f64`, `0x402e609c`) and coexists with Deja Vu V5.1, Musical V4 and Zoom V11. It also went into an elekloader-built image. It is built with plain binutils (`m68k-linux-gnu-as -mcpu=5475`). Overbridge suspected of conflicting: keep the probe build separate. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Telemetry as audio: a DSP track outputs one constant level per block (frame of 47 blocks with sync levels), recorded via an Overbridge track output. Overbridge applies a DC-blocking highpass (one pole, a = 0.9981 at 48 kHz) that the decoder must undo. About 50 % of frames decode. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Load display build: show peak cycles per call on the playhead. This is the only figure that includes real DDR stalls without a probe.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Recovery used throughout: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over DIN. Bootstrap 0x0201 is the same on 1.16 and 1.17, so the 1.16 <-> 1.17 update is reversible. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
text: digikit's flash rungs on a real DT2 1.17 (finding 47, 2026-10-18/19): each step was flashed through SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with Transfer and logged over USB SysEx. `[hw]` {digikit-f47} Rung A, the runtime in section 3 only, booted with a DIGIKIT menu. Rung B added the DSP link and voice hook (sections 3 and 7) and played stock audio. Rung C, a machine loaded at run time (pluck, 4,484 B uploaded over SysEx), halted the SHARC at the first trig. Breadcrumbs narrowed it to the step after the type match. The fix (C3d2) was to route 17 DAG-register stores through an R register, the same-DAG rule. With it, pluck played at ~1,500 dispatches/s with DSP load 41.5 -> 42 %.

section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
text: A second SHARC stop on a real DT2: `fx/freqshift` on the send route froze the unit at boot; the emulator showed nothing (findings 77, 91). Two causes were found. `[hw]` {digikit-f91} ([I15](../INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot)) A selas defect left the end of a nested hardware loop compressed (VISA). The last 11 instructions of every hardware loop must be 48-bit ISA, so wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS` ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). Code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. After both fixes, freqshift ran on the send and master routes (2026-10-30).

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
text: LFO tick `0x40139342` (caller `0x4002e912`): Parameter rows relative to A3: SPD -6, MULT -4, FADE -2, DEST 0, WAVE +2, SPH +4, MODE +6, DEP +8. WAVE is clamped to 0-6 at `0x401393c6`. WAVE 0-5 dispatch through a 6-entry table at `0x4022231c`; WAVE 6 is RAND. The table cannot be extended by appending: the RAND slew data sits right after it. The shared RNG is `(A,B) -> (B, A+B)` at `0x402b62c8/cc`. The phase increment is in D5 (signed); the stored phase is in D2. Raw WAVE 7/8 clamp to 6 and play RAND on stock. This is why Deja Vu needs two paired hooks, not one dispatch hook. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
text: Firmware heap: `malloc` at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex `0x44e08654`), `free` at `0x4011e87a` (it checks bounds and 16-byte alignment with `illegal`). The heap is a 32 MiB buddy heap `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` with metadata at `0x402b406c`. It sits inside the reset clear and initialises on first call. An 8 KiB block allocated once stayed untouched for 10 M emulated instructions. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
text: A persistent flashed cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` (2,108 B) ends exactly at the reset clear and survives boot. `0x4031be59-0x4031ff60` is inside the clear and cannot hold flashed code. The priority-6 task entry `0x40133646` is a candidate one-shot startup hook, after the heap is initialised. `[emu]` Deja Vu, the All-in-One, dt2-machine-lab and 70b185's private project all use it; who holds which bytes: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md); one freeze report: [CONFLICTS O18](../CONFLICTS.md).

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: SHARC part: ADSP-21569. Section 7 holds ADSP-2156x loader/application records (104 records mapped). FreeRTOS, an Audio task and a recurring block loop are traced. The hand-off from the boot kernel to that startup is not.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: The ColdFire <-> SHARC frame is the same shape as on the Digitone II: A full-duplex `0xabc`-byte DSPI2 frame carries a `0x802`-byte state payload: 16 records of `0x60` bytes, track n to SHARC unit n. ColdFire eDMA29 sends and eDMA28 receives; the SHARC uses SPI2 with completed-image double buffering. The send is driven from a level-5 interrupt that a level-6 eDMA-completion path forces in software. Link settings: SPI mode 1, 16-bit MSB-first, one `0x55e`-word window. The meaning of the SHARC-to-ColdFire return content is open. Compare the DN2's frame and reply words in [digitone-2-internals.md](digitone-2-internals.md). This is a second, independent reading of the shared design (research map T19).

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Project samples reach the SHARC over a different path: ColdFire Rapid-GPIO byte/strobe/ready endpoint -> SHARC link port 0 (LP0_RX, DMA30). Samples are described by five-word resource descriptors with 4 KiB pages. This agrees with digikit finding 15 ([digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md](digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md)). The physical bridge between the two endpoints is not identified.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Audio output: two 64-word banks are selected, then sent by a two-bank circular DMA descriptor (DMA10) to SPORT4 half A. Codec and pin are not identified.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Update path: MAIN validates checksum, minimum version and the cryptographic trailer before it erases and programs the staged ELE3 slot at flash `0x80000`, then requests a reset. Which updater copy runs after reset, and whether recovery is independent of it, is marked opaque.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Offline modifications proven in the simulator only: a byte-exact selector reroute, and a 3-byte change that turns an output-bank negation into pass-through. Re-encoding a modified section and running it on hardware are explicitly unproven.

section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
text: The main OS's default exception handler prints `EXCEPTION ...` with the vector, format, PC and twelve stack words, then executes `halt` with interrupts masked. It never returns.

section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
text: The core watchdog is not used anywhere in the main OS, so a fault hangs the whole device until the power is cycled. Messages like the DT2's `V04 M0 P40311A64` (dt2-machine-lab) are this handler's output.

section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
text: digikit's runtime counts bad boots: the counter is raised at boot start and cleared only after 30 s of stable running. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: The intro is its own task, priority 7, created once by the installer before the main-OS task (DT2 `0x400d1448`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3920`) and woken by a PIT3 tick. A higher number is more urgent here, so the intro preempts the main-OS task (priority 6). A frame callback that never returns starves the main OS until power-off.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Five scene tables at `0x402a1b64`, `0x402a1b74`, `0x402a1b84`, `0x402a1b94`, `0x402a1ba4`. Each boot picks one with an LCG; the first is picked about 99.9 % of the time and has 175 frames. An entry is `{callback, frame count}`, ended by a 0.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: One pointer drives it: the current entry is at DT2 `0x43153a00`, DN2 1.12 `0x42c4cacc`, DN2 1.11 `0x42c4bacc`. Only the setup function (DT2 `0x400d1832`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d0a`) and the tick function (DT2 `0x400d18f0`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3dc8`) touch it. Each frame calls `callback(index, count, bitmap)`; count 0 ends the intro the normal way: the pointer is cleared, PIT3 stops and semaphore `0x43149550` releases the main-OS task.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Swapping the intro: a hook before the setup function's argument load (`move.l (0x24,SP),D0; movea.l D0,A0`, DT2 `0x400d183a`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d12`, DN2 1.11 `0x400d3bae`, the same 6 bytes on all three) can point it at an own table. In digikit's emulator the UI was then reached after 115 audio blocks instead of 5,973 (DT2) and 6,180 (DN2). Stock's frame clear is `0x40113700` (DN2 1.12 `0x40115074`, DN2 1.11 `0x40114d94`), called as `(bitmap, 0, 1)`. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Frame rate unresolved: digikit's timer model gives 30 Hz (175 frames = 5.8 s); its earlier emulator notes derived 15 Hz. Open conflict [O20](../CONFLICTS.md). Module code first runs at about frame 53-57 of the intro (emulator); almost all of that delay is stock setup.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Faults during the intro reach stock's halting handler (see the section above): digikit installs its own crash handler only from the UI loop.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Frame layout on the panel (measured on one DT2 1.17): with y = 0 at the top, the intro bitmap holds pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, flipped vertically only. digikit's emulator shows these frames the other way up. `[hw]` ([I53](../INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel))

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Safe mode is digikit's, not stock's: REC (key `0x13`, state byte 2 bit 2; key state array at DT2 `0x44dc8644`, DN2 `0x445a2e30`) held from power-on skips all modules. On one DT2 1.17 it worked, and a custom boot screen started about 1.8 s after the stock intro. `[hw]` ([I54](../INCIDENTS.md#i54-safe-mode-by-rec-at-power-on-tested-on-a-digitakt-ii))

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: With the black intro patch set, the bootstrap's logo, "B" and the OS version stay until the main OS first writes the display, then about 1-2 s of black, then the boot screen. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: ColdFire heap: a 32 MiB buddy allocator at `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` (16-byte minimum, power-of-two blocks), parameters at `0x402b406c`.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Allocating from the stock heap at startup (digitakt-ii-research, OS 1.16, emulator, byte-verified sites) {dt2-research-heap}: `malloc` is at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex at `0x44e08654`, lazy init on first call). `free` is at `0x4011e87a`. It traps with `illegal` on a pointer outside the heap or not 16-byte aligned, the same rule as the Digitakt mk1's operator delete. The OS clears `0x40312000-0x47e28470` at reset, so static data placed there does not survive boot. A startup hook at `0x40133646` (`link.w` + `movem`) made exactly one 8 KiB allocation that stayed untouched for 20 M instructions. This is the cleanest way to own memory without a cave.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Sample pool: Logical range `0x400-0x19000400`, 400 MiB, allocations rounded to 8 KiB. The ColdFire's allocation records decide admission; no SHARC malloc is involved. In the SHARC's view the pool is a window at DSP byte address `0x8422b9c8 + (offset - 0x400)`, ending at `0x9d22b9c8`. Capicola reserves the top 8 MiB.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Recorder: the main OS fetches recorder data in chunks of at most `0x800` bytes over DSPI1 from a service whose physical owner (ColdFire, SHARC DDR or a third part) is not established. Staging buffers are at `0x4fe79340` / `0x4fe7a340`.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: SHARC side: Sample-slot table at `0x257810 + slot*0x14`: 1,025 entries, slot `0x400` is the preview. Voices at `0x2412cc + lane*0x1d8`, 32 lanes: `+0` PCM pointer, `+0x188` length, `+0x1b8` active. Link-port 0 receive staging at `0x268220` (descriptor) and `0x268240` (a tag plus 4 KiB of payload).

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Once published to the SHARC, PCM keeps playing after the ColdFire source is freed, as long as the stock allocation stays owned. Saving, however, needs the source, and no read-back path from sample memory was found.

section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
text: digikit's patchkit (used by digitakt-ii-research's All-in-One and dt2-machine-lab), elekloader's core-dt2 (used by digitakt2-perform) and the hand-placed builds share the flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000`. elekloader's RAM `0x47f00000-0x47f40000` lies inside digikit's `cf.expansion` `0x47e8b000-0x47fe0000`. Full table of ranges and hook sites: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
text: A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed a unit (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16): [firmware-container.md](../common/firmware-container.md), rule A46. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-capicola} ([I16](../INCIDENTS.md#i16-a-decoded-section-7-over-1-mib-crashed-the-unit))

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Reading a track's Sound parameter words needs no fixed address: get the project singleton, its ProjectSettings at project + `0x30` (static analysis only), the selected track from `view_track` (clamped 0-15), then `native_track_sound(active kit, track)` = kit + `0x6c` + `0x3c0` x track; vtable slot `0x28` of that Sound object returns the record pointer `*(sound + 0x10)` (0 when none is bound), and word i is a big-endian s16 at record + `0x14` + 2i. Anchors: settings `0x40041d18` (DT2 1.17) / `0x4003e40e` (DN2 1.12); `native_track_sound` `0x40035cca` / `0x40030e66`. The array holds 71 words on the DT2 and 101 on the DN2. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: On the DN2 a track's Sound record can sit at an odd address (kit stride `0x48b`), so read it byte by byte. A parameter code maps to its array index through the descriptor table (rows of `0x3c` bytes, index as s32 at row + 4, -1 = no word); the same index means another parameter on another machine. P-locks, sound lock, LFO and MIDI CC writes go through other paths, and a latched parameter of a run-time machine changed no word in the array (where it is stored is open). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Track overdrive (stock): the curve clamps to +-1 and applies y*(2-|y|) three times; the blend is x + mix*(y-x) with stock ramps for drive and mix. OVR Routing is parameter `0x103` (Sound mirror index 68; 0 = pre, `0x100` = post). The per-track stage is called twice per track from the voice chain. `[doc]` {digikit-overdrive}

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Run-time machines: on the DT2 they can use knob slots B C E F G H; a parameter on the seventh slot replaces LEV, whose level is then fixed at 100. The run-time module stage is limited to 64 KB; a TB-303 port costs about 8,000 SHARC instructions per 32-sample block. `[doc]` {digikit-tb303}

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: ColdFire jump targets must be even: a jsr/jmp to an odd address faults with an address error on the unit while the emulator runs on; a byte-aligned mod section froze a DT2 at boot (I61). `[hw]` {elekloader-oddjump}

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Modwerk's DT2 base: a combined image booted on a DT2 (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08) and restored saved module kit data after a project reload. Its audio scheduler (grid callbacks and phrase replacement at the stock audio submission call `0x400d82f8`) is a proposal checked only in digikit fixtures. `[hw]` / `[emu]` {modwerk-dt2-base}

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: The firmware's own file calls can write samples: open (`0x40158902`, mode "w"), write (`0x4015866a`), reserve, hash (`0x4015b3aa`), close (`0x401588c0`), info, delete (`0x40157078`), mkdir and rename (`0x40156f6c`, which keeps the inode, size and stored hash). Each takes the recursive filesystem mutex itself and blocks, so call them from a task, never an interrupt. The sampler's recorder `0x40153c70` is a complete stock caller. `[doc]` (static)

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: Open does not truncate: an existing file opens at position 0 with its old size and data; stock deletes first. Whole 32 KiB pages at multiples of `0x8000` are written straight from the buffer, the rest goes through the page cache. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: The 16-byte trailer: files carry 16 zero bytes after the data, and the stored hash covers them; the C calls do not add them (the recorder and stock's MidiRpc close do), so a writer adds them before the hash. File info reports size minus 16. `[emu]` (card read back on the emulator) Elekloader's Rytm loader meets the same 16 bytes as a header at the start of each file on the Analog Rytm MKII ([analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: Power cut: a cut mid-write leaves a visible file with a partial size and no hash; the mount was not seen to repair it. Delete refuses an open file (open-file bitmap at `0x46f4ded0`). Only `/factory` is RAM-backed; user files always go to the card, and a failed card write is not reported. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: On a unit (2026-11-11) digikit's bulk uploads through these calls left only complete files after a pulled cable, and the stock sample browser did not list the staging folder `/.dkstage`. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

section: Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
text: In RAM: the project object is at `0x41776c9c`; 128 patterns from `0x41776cb8` (stride `0x1db8c`), 128 kits from `0x426532b8` (stride `0x5574`). Serializer `0x400df66c` (flag bits pick the parts), loader `0x400df95a`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
text: Bytes the serializer never writes: pattern record `0x15acc-0x15c00`, kit record `0x573e-0x5800`, file header `0x1c-0x200`. Pattern RAM `+0x1cef0..0x1db60` is not saved but is in use: pokes there hung the UI. `[doc]` (the hang `[hw]`)

section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
text: Whole-sample-clear hook on OS 1.17: the entry `0x40154634` starts with push A2, push D2, `clr.l D2` (6 bytes); a hook resumes at `0x4015463a`. INIT NEW and a full project LOAD both pass it. It is a notice, not a promise that the recorder, loaders or DMA have stopped: drain your own work before stock frees the backing. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
text: OS 1.16 project LOAD: the stock clear runs once per sample slot, so it marks no project boundary; the post-clear sample-batch entry does. The load-and-select callback (caller `0x40046c8e`) saves a recovery copy to internal slot 128 before its asynchronous sample batch completes; a mod that blocks that save makes LOAD report LOAD ERROR although decoding succeeded (I93). `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
text: Sample rows are shared: digikit's `core/sample-pool` reserves the top sixteen rows (H112-H127); Sketch uses H124-H127 for live buffers and H116-H123 for FREEZE, so the two declare a conflict. A user sample in those rows also blocks the reservation. Two mods that reserve sample rows need one owner. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
text: OS 1.16 recorder editor (static): the waveform service `0x4001266a` issues recorder command 3 for four signed extrema; encoder handling at `0x40020960`; trim endpoints at view +`0x9a0`/+`0x9a4`; the accepted-range copy is command 4 at `0x4001282e`. The native accept refuses ranges below 141 frames. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
text: Stock SHARC load on OS 1.16 (emulator, mean instructions per 32-frame block of 666,667 cycles): 206,144 idle, 209,769 with 1 stereo track, 220,304 with 4, 262,231 with 16. Bounded workloads, not worst cases. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
text: Pointer returns: the firmware returns pointers in d0, while GCC's m68k ABI reads them from a0; a C prototype returning a pointer froze the UI. Declare such routines as returning a 32-bit integer. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
text: Sites: encoder filter `0x40111cda`; per-frame value block `0x80005b50`; modulator call site `0x4002e90c`; LED frame `0x4003117c`, LED setter `0x400308e0`; NameView wrapper `0x40117c70`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
text: LED colour byte: on a unit `0x31` looked deep blue and `0x41` yellow (one observer, by eye); this disagrees with digikit's own finding 19 (CONFLICTS O25). `[hw]` `[?]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: USB mode switch: `FUN_40006c16` has the same address and bytes on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. It takes no lock and cuts a MIDI reply in flight; USB restarts after a 30-tick counter (about 1 s in the emulator; counter DT2 `0x40965a38`, DN2 `0x4058f280`). The stored USB CONFIG byte (0 MIDI, 1 Overbridge, 2 AUDIO/MIDI; DT2 `0x4099d5c4`, DN2 `0x405ce898`) is written only by the menu actions (DT2 `0x4010331a`/`30`/`48`, DN2 `0x40104dc2`/`d8`/`f0`), never by the switch, so a reboot returns to the stored mode; an Overbridge disconnect (`FUN_400f2ce0`) is the only path that re-applies it by itself. DT2 connection-state word `0x40965a40`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Take-over on units (2026-11-11): digikit's Fast USB switched both units from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM for an upload over its bulk interface and back (SysEx TAKEOVER `0x1e`, RELEASE `0x1f`); the stored mode byte stayed unchanged and USB audio was heard working afterwards. Longer loops later lost a unit from USB (I80, next section). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: +Drive internals: close hash `0x4015b1e8` under the filesystem mutex `0x46f4deb0` (recursive lock `0x400015a0`, unlock `0x400016d2`); inode get/put/write `0x4015b92a`/`0x4015b846`/`0x4015b868`; extent lookup `0x4015813c`; hash-table rebuild `0x4015b0ee` (about 300 ms per file on a unit); event post `0x4015a6aa`. Data page 0 is card sector `0x5ee180` (page p at base + p x `0x40`), the first hash page sector `0x5ee980`. Every file write reaches the card before the call returns. The eSDHC read/write is clamped to 64 KiB (DT2 `0x4012e3c4`, DN2 `0x4012ca8a`). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Measured ceilings (8 MiB, 2026-11-11): DT2 +Drive file write 2.6 MB/s with 64 KiB calls, 7.8 MB/s with 256 KiB, 10.3 MB/s with 1 MiB; the firmware's close-hash re-read 4.2 MB/s; store writes DT2 about 7.2 MB/s, DN2 6.3 MB/s; raw card reads 15.3 MB/s on both; CPU hash 16-18.7 MB/s. A whole 8 MB upload: DT2 2.99-6.15 s (varies a lot between runs), DN2 1.75 s. Per file about 0.18-0.19 s fixed cost. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Fast close: digikit hashes from a card read-back and then runs the firmware's own close steps, byte-identical to the stock close, falling back to the firmware close if the read-back fails. After such uploads the stock browser listed the files, a sample loaded and played, and a project that referenced an uploaded sample reloaded and played it. Creating the staging folder `/.dkstage` cost about 420 ms and removing a file from it about 150 ms, so it now stays for the session. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: SHARC cycle counter: each image has exactly one EMUCLK reader, the block handler (DT2 `0x1c74cd`, DN2 `0x1c9d6b`), which keeps a low-word delta for reporting only; nothing branches on it. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: eMMC EXT_CSD copy in RAM: DT2 1.17 `0x4fe69100`, DN2 1.12 `0x4e6f9100`; bytes are reversed within each 32-bit word because the eSDHC runs little-endian. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: The USB mode take-over is not reliable on a unit: switching a Digitakt II from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM and back lost the unit from USB in cycle 5 of a 20-cycle loop, and in cycle 11 after digikit added a 2 s restart hold and parked the PHY's line during the stop. The host saw no disconnect, the unit no longer answered, a cable replug did not help and only a power cycle did; both failures came on TAKEOVER, never on RELEASE. digikit now keeps the take-over off by default; with USB CONFIG set to USB MIDI in the menu its fast transfer ran fully reliably (I80, rule A55). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: External ULPI PHY: the USB controller drives an external ULPI PHY (PORTSC.PTS = ULPI, set at init `0x40006d1c`-`0x40006d2c`). The stock firmware writes no PHY register: its only ULPI_VIEWPORT (`0xFC0B0170`) use is a read of PHY register 0 every 300 calls of a periodic function (`0x40006af8`), which resets the controller (not the PHY) when the read never finishes. It never sets PORTSC.PHCD. The VBUS interrupt (`0x40005e14`, OTGSC.BSVIS) starts or stops the controller; the restart `0x40006bc6` starts it only while OTGSC.BSV is set. Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: The USB clock comes from the PHY: the stock init clears MISCCR.USBSRC (`0xEC09000E` bit 0), so the PHY's 60 MHz ULPI output clocks the controller's USB side. A PHY whose clock stops freezes USB while the rest of the unit runs on. The documented way to restart a stopped PHY clock is a viewport wake-up (WU set, RUN clear). Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: Stock controller reset: `0x40006ada` (same on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12) stops the controller with restart type 2; after 30 ticks `0x40007104` sets USBCMD.RST and spins on it with no bound, runs the USB init `0x40006c52` and restarts if VBUS is valid. The firmware's own viewport watchdog uses this path. Each reset leaks one of the 16 shared timer slots (SB20). `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: How a failed take-over looks: after RS is set again PORTSC shows line state SE0 (`0xa0000005`; good switches show J), no SOF arrives and the host never addresses the device; after a controller reset OTGSC.BSV reads 0. Failures came on take-over and on release, with audio idle: 1 in 76 and 1 in 200 switches on two builds; parking the PHY line during the stop made it about 1 in 15. A replug never helped, a power cycle always did; a stop/hold/restart and the stock reset did not revive it. A viewport wake-up was never tried on a unit (I80). `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: USB AUDIO/MIDI port entry 5: the port table has 0x28-byte entries; entry 5 is at table + 0xC8 (DT2 `0x4029f048`): +0 connect `0x400040a6`, +4 disconnect `0x40004054`, +0xC configuration pointer, +0x10 length 0x148. The configuration has 5 interfaces (UAC2 on 0-2, MIDI on 3-4 with the EP1 bulk pair); EP2 IN is the iso feedback and EP2 OUT is unused. A bus reset clears ENDPTCTRL1-3 and every queue head, and SET_CONFIGURATION calls connect again. DN2 1.12 has the same code at other data addresses. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: A bulk OUT endpoint fits beside live USB audio: digikit hooks the USB init entry `0x40006c52` (6-byte prologue, same on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12; it runs at boot and again in interrupt context after a controller reset), copies the configuration, appends interface 5 (vendor class, EP2 OUT bulk, 512 bytes), sets wTotalLength 0x158 and repoints entry 5; connect and disconnect touch only the receive half of ENDPTCTRL2. Replies go back over SysEx. A probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads on 2026-11-13: DN2 3.38 MB/s (6.5 MB) and 2.09 MB/s (146 MB in 200 files, audio clean), DT2 2.74 and 1.50 MB/s. macOS keeps audio and MIDI; Windows does not bind it without an MS OS 2.0 descriptor. Not yet tested: long runs, host sleep, a bus reset during a transfer. `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: eMMC: both units carry an eMMC 5.1 of 23.05 GiB with identical EXT_CSD: enhanced reliable write supported but not forced, 1 MiB cache off, background operations off, optimal write size 32 KiB. Card clock 37.71 MHz (75.43 MHz divided by 2) on a 4-bit bus in high-speed timing; the eSDHC has no 8-bit mode. `[hw]` (read on the units)

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: Stock card driver: data moves by eDMA channel 59 to the eSDHC data port, 16 bytes per request; every write uses CMD23 with the reliable-write bit. The block write and read split every transfer into 64 KiB commands: `cmpi.l #0x10000,D2` at offset 0x14 (entry) and 0x22 (chunk loop) of each function, same bytes on both images: DT2 1.17 read `0x4012e1b6` (sites `0x4012e1ca`, `0x4012e1d8`), write `0x4012e39c` (sites `0x4012e3b0`, `0x4012e3be`); DN2 1.12 read `0x4012c87a` (`0x4012c88e`, `0x4012c89c`), write `0x4012ca60` (`0x4012ca74`, `0x4012ca82`). The 64 KiB bounce buffer for unaligned buffers is the likely reason; the eDMA's 15-bit count allows at most 1023 blocks (511 KiB) a command, which digikit's sdhc-large uses (1022) for 16-byte aligned buffers it registers. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: Raw card rates (DN2, 8 MiB, median of 3): write 11.4 / 13.3 / 15.3 MB/s and read 13.8 / 15.6 / 16.1 MB/s with 32 KiB / 64 KiB / 511 KiB commands; reliable write and the card cache change nothing within 2 %. A copy in RAM runs at 18 MB/s, USB alone at 20.9 MB/s (13.5 MB/s while the CPU copies). An upload that reads every file back is capped at about 7.2-7.8 MB/s by the card. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: Cost per file: on the DN2 store the cost of an upload grows by about 0.46 ms for each file already stored (the store table is rewritten and read back at every commit), on top of about 95 ms; on the DT2 +Drive about 195 ms a file, with no growth across folders. For sample packs of hundreds of files this matters more than the transfer rate. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
text: +Drive ids at or above `0x1000000` never reach the card (DT2 1.17): the inode write-back `0x4015b868` and page write-back `0x40155c34` call the block write only for inode ids and page numbers below `0x1000000`; higher ones are copied into RAM tables (inodes at `0x47d73ed0 + n*0x80`, pages at `0x46f63ed0 + n*0x8000`, n counted from `0x1000000`). `[doc]` {digikit-f120}

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: NRPN numbers disagree between the OS 1.17 manual and midi.guide's data for track mute and level, pattern mute, master overdrive, filter env depth, filter base/width and portamento; all CCs agree (CONFLICTS O24). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: CC 80 (amp HOLD) at 127 switches HOLD to NOTE; it is not the longest hold. A sound ends on note-off only with AMP MODE = ADSR or HOLD = NOTE. Note 60 plays a sample at its own pitch only with TUNE 64 and the preset OCTAVE unchanged. No CC or NRPN selects the machine type. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: CC 19 selects the sample slot from the project pool; it switched slots audibly on a unit (2026-11-11). MIDI Start also starts the unit's own sequencer, so the selected pattern's trigs play on top of an external part. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: USB audio: class-compliant audio exists only in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode, with one stereo USB OUT pair; track outputs over USB carry no effects; INT TO MAIN = AUTO mutes the internal outs while USB audio streams. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Pre-send render hook proposal (Modwerk, OS 1.17, emulator)
text: Modwerk's proposal guards the SHARC send-driver entry `0x1c18a6` (short-word PC), displacing one 6-byte instruction and resuming at `0x1c18a9`; the stock caller is at `0x1c3090`. Track buses start at DM `0x252df8`, 256 bytes a track, 32 floats per channel. A sidechain prototype (16 sources x 16 destinations) ran 9,060 SHARC instructions a block in digikit's emulator; with the hook off the PCM was byte-identical to stock. Not on a unit. `[emu]`

Find a screen from the frame the OS has just drawn instead (I106). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB MIDI callbacks and Shot's cost (digikit handover, 2026-11-15)
text: The function at `0x4000434a` stores two USB MIDI callbacks into .bss slots: `0x409659d0` / `0x409659d4` on the Digitakt II (1.17), `0x4058f218` / `0x4058f21c` on the Digitone II 1.12. USB MIDI that arrives before they are set leaves the link dead while the CPU runs (an emulator-only failure in digikit's tests). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB MIDI callbacks and Shot's cost (digikit handover, 2026-11-15)
text: digikit's Shot sample machine costs about 5,057 (DT2) / 5,266 (DN2) instructions per 32-frame block; 16 voices use 91 % of the DN2 headroom. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and the bus timer (digikit findings 07 and 132, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Every ColdFire task switch passes through `vector_32_handler` at `0x40000410` (20,760 entries on DT2 and 17,778 on DN2 over the probe window). Vector 205 is the switch entered from an interrupt, always from stacked IPL 0; vector 32 (`trap #0`) is a task yielding, with SR 0x2700; vector 191 does not occur, and no switch is entered from a handler at IPL 2 or higher. So code reachable from a task needs an entry/exit counter before it can be unloaded while running; code reached only from interrupts can be unloaded after masking interrupts and clearing its slot. `[emu]` (PC probe)

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and the bus timer (digikit findings 07 and 132, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Main-OS entry comes at instruction 299,258,200 on DT2 and 298,782,809 on DN2. `param_code` runs before it, from the boot project decode loop (caller DT2 `FUN_400e64dc`, return `0x400e6546`; DN2 `FUN_400e7eb0`, return `0x400e7f1a`), and saw only stock machine types even with a saved project that uses digikit's types 16/17: the saved project loads after main-OS entry, so hooks installed there are early enough. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and the bus timer (digikit findings 07 and 132, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: DTIM0's counter `DTCN0` at `0xfc07000c` runs at the 132 MHz bus clock, 88,000 ticks per 32-sample frame, and is already running before the main OS. digikit uses it read-only as its profiling clock (`span_clock` in the device files). The rate was measured on the owner's unit on 2026-11-07 (the source does not say which device). `[hw]` The Analog Rytm MKII's DTCN0 runs at the same rate ([analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: One card transfer at a time: the eSDHC has one command and one data channel, no command queue and no packed commands; it supports SD Host 2.0 and MMC 4.2 only (no DDR), and the 8-bit pins are not bonded. The reference manual gives 40 MHz as the eSDHC maximum; the firmware runs 37.7 MHz (SDCLKFS=1, DVS=0, DT2 setup `0x4012d78e`). A command without data (CMD13) can go out during a data transfer, but errata SECF214 says it may see a spurious CRC or index error. FIFO 128 x 32 bit; the controller stops the card clock on FIFO under- or overrun. Wire ceiling about 18.5 MB/s payload, about 9.3 MB/s for write plus full read-back. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: Stock card driver locking: every block transfer runs under one global mutex (DT2 `0x47de3cac`) plus a second mutex `0x44e4ae98` taken through `0x401344dc`; a request above 64 KiB is cut into 64 KiB chunks, each locked on its own. The caller starts eDMA channel 59 and waits with `sem_pend` on `0x44e3fec8` (command complete) and `0x44e3fec0` / `0x44e3feb8` (data); the eSDHC ISR `0x4012d5ba` (vector 223) posts `0x44e3fec8` on CC/CTOE and `0x44e3fec0` on TC or a data error (the poster of `0x44e3feb8` was not found). The task sleeps during DMA and card busy, so other tasks get the CPU. Reads use CMD18 with auto-CMD12 and no CMD23; writes send CMD23 with the reliable-write bit before every CMD25, no auto-CMD12. Setup: CMD6 HS_TIMING=1, BUS_WIDTH=1 (4 bit), ERASE_GROUP_DEF=1, CMD16 512; no cache enable or flush, packed commands or command queue seen. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: RTOS primitives (DT2 1.17; the DN2 1.12 mutex functions sit at the same addresses): priority-preemptive, a larger number is a higher priority; task switch by `trap #0` (`0x40000410`); no tick that rotates tasks of equal priority was found `[?]`. Binary semaphores `sem_init` `0x40001398`, `sem_pend` `0x4000141a`, `sem_post` `0x4000155c` (a counting variant at `0x4000148c`, `0x400014fc`, `0x4000172a`). Mutexes `0x400015a0` / `0x400016d2` are recursive for the owner with FIFO waiters and no priority inheritance. No task delete, yield or event flags were found. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: +Drive serialises as well: every `file.*` and `path.*` call runs under the file-system mutex `0x46f4deb0`, and the close (`0x4015b3aa` -> `0x4015b1e8`) holds it through the whole read-back and hash-table work. Several files can be open (open bitmap `0x46f4ded0`), but they share static scratch buffers (`0x4066d8c0`, `0x406658c0`, `0x44f2bc68`). So several writers (tasks, files or pieces of one file) cannot raise card throughput; a pipeline (one task waits on the card while another copies or hashes in RAM) is safe and helps. Keep middle-priority work from delaying the task that holds the card mutex. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: +Drive page allocation (DT2 1.17): `file_reserve` `0x40158810` calls `0x40158448(id, 0, bytes, 0)`: inode get, missing-page count `0x40158326`, free-page count `0x40155f84` (bit by bit over the 0x14010-byte bitmap, no I/O), then `0x401581dc(inode, 0, pages, 0)` and the inode write-back `0x4015b868`. `0x401581dc` allocates first fit with `0x40155974` from page `0xa7a`, then from 0, writes the touched bitmap pages and adds one extent per allocation (`0x40157c68`); it stops silently when no page is free and does not write the inode back. Call it under the file-system mutex with an inode from inode get, hint 0. `[doc]` {digikit-f120}

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: Where upload time goes (2026-11-16, every file hash-checked on the unit): one 9.8 MB file: DN2 3.66-3.73 MB/s (card writes 710 ms = 13.8 MB/s, copy from the USB buffers 710 ms, END with read-back, hash and commit 1100 ms); DT2 3.46-3.52 MB/s (BEGIN 141 ms, card writes 988 ms = 9.9 MB/s, copy 558 ms, END 1009 ms of which read-back 940 ms = 10.4 MB/s). A 309-file pack (1.05 MB a file): on the DN2 the END per file grew from 386 to 550 ms between two runs as the store filled (about 300-480 ms of it is the store-table commit); on the DT2 per file `file_reserve` 94 ms (also 90 ms for the 9.8 MB file), `path_open "w"` 52 ms, rename 56 ms, read-back hash 92 ms (32 KiB pages), the 16-byte trailer write 13 ms. The DT2's fixed cost of about 200 ms a file stays flat up to 618 files in one folder. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: Cached USB receive is slower: reading the USB receive buffers through the cached window (with a cache-line invalidate before the read) gave 3.47-3.50 MB/s against 3.66-3.73 MB/s uncached on a DN2; the copy time stayed about 0.71 s, and the extra 0.19 s is likely the about 600,000 line invalidates per 9.8 MB. Why the copy runs at only about 14 MB/s is open. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: What did help (all kept since runtime 0.8.3): one store-table commit for up to 16 files took a DN2 100-file pack from 2.42 to 3.25 MB/s, and 3.56 with copy/write overlap; overlap alone (a helper task copies into one 512 KiB half while the card writes the other) took a 9.8 MB file from 3.67 to 4.37 MB/s (DN2) and 3.53 to 4.01 MB/s (DT2). On the DT2, read-back in runs of up to 128 KiB, the trailer in the last write, page allocation without the free-page count and new files written at their final name (no rename; a power cut can leave one partial unhashed file visible) took a pack from 2.32 to 2.49 MB/s, and 3.07 MB/s with every lever; the 9.8 MB file reached 4.13 MB/s with read-back runs, trailer and overlap. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: CACR and the by-address flush: both images write CACR once, at `0x4000055a` (`move.l #0xa50ce100,d0`: SPA=1, IVO=0, DDPI=0, IDPI=0, instruction and data cache on). With SPA=1, `cpushl bc,(ax)` searches by physical address and clears the line in both caches (RM Table 6-10), so one `cpushl` per 16-byte line is a correct flush for new code. Do not write CACR yourself. Whether a pipeline sync is needed after the last `cpushl` is open. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: The task that loads a project: DT2 entry `0x400caff0` (created at `0x400cc7ce`, TCB `0x4039be58`, priority 2, stack `0x4039beac` + `0x4000`); DN2 entry `0x400cd5f2` (created at `0x400cec02`, TCB `0x40386e48`). It reaches `write_live_project` `0x400df95a`, `fx_array.load` `0x400daf54` and the sound-load exit; `fx_array.save` is reached from the UI side (`0x400dbdca`). This is call-graph reachability only (vtable calls are not edges). `[?]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: The UI task and its queue: DT2 `main_os_task` `0x400337ba` (created at `0x40033280`, TCB `0x40966ee8`, priority 6, stack `0x4096775c` + `0x28000`) waits on queue `0x40966f3c` (wait function `0x40001928`) and switches on the message byte; the UI-loop site is `0x40033d06`. DN2: entry `0x4002ed34`, created at `0x4002e902`, TCB `0x4059e1c0`, queue `0x4059e214`, site `0x4002f17e`. No other code reads that queue, so modal pop-ups and browsers run inside message handlers and a UI-loop hook runs once per message. A7 inside one of the two stacks tells which task runs a hook. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: Two level-7 interrupts (not maskable): INTC0 ICR2 (`0xfc048042`, set at `0x40001cbe`): EPF2, vector 0x108, handler `0x40001a10`, a 516-byte leaf with no callees. INTC1 ICR40 (`0xfc04c068`, set at `0x400d346e`): EDMA_INTR, its handler installed at run time into vector 0x2a0 from pointer `0x43153a2c` (DN2 sites `0x400d56c6`, `0x400d5996`); which code it runs is open. An IPL-7 mask therefore does not keep these two out. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: Empty machine rows and the name table: stock `mf_dispatch` `0x400c89a4` uses `type < 7 ? 0x4293b960 + 0x2c * type : 0x4293ba68`, so a stored type on an empty row plays as type 0. No code keeps a pointer to a name-table row (only `lea` in the accessors); the machine list is fetched once into the view at boot. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: The boot intro drops stock MidiRpc: after a restart digikit's runtime answered at once, but the firmware was still on its boot intro and dropped stock MidiRpc file requests; digikit's host now probes read-only for up to about 30 s and never resends a write (I114). `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
text: Encoder input needs fast detents: digikit reports that the firmware encoder needs fast detents (12 detents moved a value about one or two steps); its test helpers send 4-detent events 30 ms apart. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)
text: The six `type == 6` (MANUAL SLICE) tests on DT2 1.17, for anyone who clones MANUAL SLICE: `0x4005fbec` (`moveq #6,D1; cmp.l D0,D1; beq.w`, target `0x4005fcd4`), `0x4005f8f8` (`bne.b`, target `0x4005f920`), `0x40030e1e` (`bne.w`, target `0x40030f90`), `0x4004923e` (D6 holds 6, target `0x40049266`), `0x4005c936` (type in D2, target `0x4005c950`) and in the frame builder `0x4002ec18` (`mvs.b (0x990,A0),D0`, target `0x4002ecd8`). digikit removed its hooks there on 2026-11-18 because no machine of theirs clones MANUAL SLICE. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)
text: The masked test `(type & ~2) == 4` is at `0x4005da60` (12 bytes; first four instructions); its `beq.w` target is `0x4005db02`. digikit maps an added type to its `clone_of` there. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)
text: MANUAL SLICE's slice table (frame words `+0xee..+0xf8`) is sent only for type 6, so a clone of SAMPLE gets none. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)
text: The VerticalMenuView font is not at a fixed field offset: the field offset differs between firmwares, so read the font from the `move.l #font,D0` literal in the constructor (6 bytes at constructor + `0xb6`): DT2 1.17 `0x4011a022`, DN2 1.12 `0x4011b996`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)
text: SHARC pointer-slot stubs: digikit's image now jumps from each SHARC hook through one of 16 words in window 0 of its DSP link area (zero = stock path). Measured in its SHARC rig: 6 instructions per FX hook with an empty slot; an empty FX chain with the service 27 instructions, one disabled row 206. About +10 instructions per voice on DT2 for the voice stub and dispatch. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)
text: ColdFire pointer-slot stubs (pattern): 12 bytes per site (`movea.l slot,aN; tst.l aN; beq.b; jmp (aN)`, or `move.l slot,dN; beq.b; move.l dN,-(sp); rts`); the installer writes the slot word under IPL 7 and then flushes the cache line. A displaced instruction with a `(d8,PC,Xn)` operand cannot be re-encoded and needs a hand-written tail. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Modwerk's Digitakt II plan (GOAL.md, OS 1.17, 2026-11-16)
text: USB MIDI in every USB mode: OS 1.17 offers USB MIDI in MIDI, Audio/MIDI and Overbridge modes, so a SysEx link over it needs no change to the USB descriptors. Modwerk reports that the stock transmit path can wait indefinitely for buffer space, so a link reply must not block when the host stops reading. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Modwerk's Digitakt II plan (GOAL.md, OS 1.17, 2026-11-16)
text: Kit data room: a kit record holds 191 bytes of kit data for all mods together (core 1.1; 143 B on Modwerk's base, see 2026-11-17 below {modwerk-1118}). Open: whether OS 1.17 saves a kit when only a mod's block changed (H20). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Modwerk's Digitakt II plan (GOAL.md, OS 1.17, 2026-11-16)
text: Recovery floor: FUNC + TRIG 4 at power-on, then the stock `.syx` over MIDI DIN. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Modwerk base 8650bb8a, Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08..17)
text: Kit-data room is 143 B on Modwerk's base: core 1.1 gives 191 B (`KIT_ROOM` 194), but Modwerk's project archive uses the last 48 B of each serialized kit record, so the base ends core's kit data at `0x57d0` (`KIT_ROOM` 146). On base `e88273ed` the two overlapped and a save zeroed the archive (I147). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Modwerk base 8650bb8a, Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08..17)
text: Official OS 1.17 opened a project saved on base `8650bb8a` with Chord Arp, Euclidean Scale and Track Names; on the modded build all settings survived Save Project and a power cycle. `[hw]` (one unit)

section: Digitakt II / Modwerk base 8650bb8a, Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08..17)
text: Core 1.1 storage sites (stock bytes guarded): kit save `0x400dbee4`, kit load `0x400db8be`, project save `0x400df932`, project load `0x400df99c`, `memcpy` `0x40136388`, key-LED frame call `0x400311a2`. Modwerk base: 22 sites, 10,032 B `.run` + 9,848 B `.bss` (19,880 B) in the shared DDR. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Where the audio runs (Digiwerk prior-art survey, 2026-10)
text: The Digitakt mk1 renders all its audio on the ColdFire itself, in the render interrupt (vector 191). It has no DSP chip. New machines and filters (DigiFilter, digistring, digisophie, digineighbor, digislicer) are ColdFire C built with `m68k-elf-gcc -mcpu=54455`, hooked in the render ISR through elekloader. `[doc]`
