section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings (2026-11-16/17)
text: Analog BD's 808 has no rest path: it runs its whole sample loop every block, triggered or not; a never-triggered 808 voice was reported at about 152 DSP instructions per sample (emulator). The 909 rests at 3. `[emu]` {modwerk-1117}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Boot order on stock 1.40C (instruction counts in octabam's emulator): the boot site `0x4000050c` calls `0x40001e50`, the DSP bootstrap upload, before the OS (4.27 M); SRAM init `0x40000512` (4.35 M); RTOS handoff with 10 tasks (10.2 M); main's last init call `0x4001fc96` (44.9 M); USB controller init `0x4001e030`, run once (45.3 M); the card's first mount `0x40061734` in the sys task (45.8 M); first UI tick that shop mods hook `0x4005595c` (45.9 M); remount (57.6 M); LOAD PROJECT, the engine task's first job (57.6 M); first audio frame (101 M). `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Files read correctly at the first mount: a probe opened and read a 16-byte and a 256 KB file with core's file calls there; the engine task had not run a job yet. USB is composed at the controller's init, before the mount, so USB mods cannot be loaded from the card. `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Code run before the mount: USB init `0x4001dfbc..0x4001e042` and its descriptors `0x400e2000..0x400e21e0` run or are read once; main's bank-pointer store `0x4001fbd0` once; `0x40025aa2` / `0x40025ac2` (the defaults routine) also in every project load; `0x4009d1de` again later. The OS changes data in its image before the mount, so a loader that needs stock bytes keeps its own copy of `0x400b9000..0x400e2324` from boot (I118, A69). `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: The DSP payloads are gone from RAM by the mount: A (`0x400e2324`, 79,563 bytes) and B (`0x400f59ef`, 77,061 bytes) are uploaded before the OS starts; by the first mount 76,702 and 73,982 of their bytes read `0xFF`. A payload patch applied later changes nothing. `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Tasks: main (TCB `0x46c7ae84`) and ten others with fixed TCBs and stacks (voice, p2a, p2b, p2c, engine, p1b, sys; sys creates storage, keyrepeat and ui); task create `0x400005fc`, current TCB at `0x800068fc`; a TCB keeps its SP at +72. The sys task's own stack holds return addresses into the card-mount path (`0x40061648`). `[doc]` (read from octabam's RTOS model)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Other routines: FAT opendir `0x46c8240e` and readdir `0x46c8244e`; stock YES/NO dialog `0x4006d57c`; the ColdFire soft reset is RCR `0xFC0A0000` = `0x80`. Stock never restarts itself (an OS upgrade asks for a power cycle); whether a unit comes back from that soft reset is not tested. `[doc]` / `[?]` (reset)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Sample arena: 14,602 pages of 6,144 bytes; TELOS's area (2 MB), staging (256 KB) and heap (768 KB) take about 3 MB of it. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Run-time DSP code (dspload-ot 0.2, from octabam's demand loader): code goes in the window gap `P:0x33dab..0x33fff` (597 words for all mods), after four slot pairs at `x:$33da3`. The ColdFire pump sends 100 halfwords a frame, only on frames whose ping word `0x800000e0` is 0, to core 1's `X:0x2901..` and rings `0xa55a` at `X:0x2900`; each block goes three times, 30 quiet frames apart. Core 0 is never written (a transfer there stalls its chain). Core 1's copier sits in SPATIALIZER's words `P:0x868-0x96c`, hooked at payload B's frame head `P:0x76`; core 0 calls bound slots from `ev_dsp_rx`. `[emu]` (not run on a unit)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: A reverb past its default knobs can write above `0x33da3`: the gap is above everything stock effects write with default settings only; dspload-ot puts a guard word (`0xc0ffee`) at each end of a block and unbinds the slot when one changes. A write that lands inside a block without touching either guard is not caught. `[doc]` (O31)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Compiler and emulator disagree on two ColdFire patterns: for `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` GCC assumes the destination uses the old a0, ot_emu the new one; for a byte push to `-(sp)` GCC assumes SP moves by 1, ot_emu by 2. Which one the CPU takes is not checked; TELOS avoids both (`-fno-ipa-sra`, `dl_memcpy` out of line). `[emu]` (I117)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Custom LFO design in the Part (Octatrack Manager user guide, 2026-11-16)
text: Each audio and MIDI track's custom LFO shape is 16 steps, each a value -128..127 and a mode, smooth or stepped (the Part's interpolation mask). A smooth step slopes linearly to the next, and step 16 slopes into step 1. On the device a step is made smooth by holding its trig and pressing TEMPO. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Custom LFO design in the Part (Octatrack Manager user guide, 2026-11-16)
text: Stock Invert maps v to -1 - v (127 becomes -128, 0 becomes -1) and keeps the modes; stock Clear sets every value to 0 and every step to stepped. The tool copies both behaviours; its hardware comparison cases (PE356/PE357) have no published result yet. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Banks in RAM: all 16 banks are resident. Bank n at `0x400e21e0 + n*0x9b340`, pattern p's slab at `+ p*0x8ed8`: 8 audio track records of `0x91a` B at `t*0x91a`, 8 MIDI records of `0x8b0` B at `0x48d0 + m*0x8b0`. Slab trailer: `+0x8e50` master length (u16, -1 = INF), `+0x8e52` master scale, `+0x8e53/54` pattern length / scale, `+0x8e55` scale mode, `+0x8e56` CHAIN AFTER (< 0 = the project's `0x8000004e`; steps from table `0x400d80dc`), `+0x8e57` Part link, `+0x8e58` tempo. The 4 working Parts (`0x18b2` B each) start at bank `+0x8ed80`, SAVE PART copies at `+0x9504a`, Part-saved flags `+0x9b312`, Part-edited byte `+0x95048`, bank-changed `+0x9b332`. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Track record: self-contained; stock's track paste copies it anywhere. P-locks at `+0x59` (64 x 32 B, `0xff` = none) hold scene-parameter indices and the sample lock is a slot number, so a moved sequence plays through the destination's Part. Trig words `+0x89a`, own length / scale `+0x50/+0x51` (MIDI `+0x28/+0x29`). Byte `+0x899` and the slab tail `+0x8e5c..+0x8ed7` are never written to the bank file (TRAC is 2,329 B on the card): leave them out when you compare RAM with a card copy. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Part slice of an audio track (what stock TRACK COPY carries, 136 B): FX1 / FX2 id `+0x00+t` / `+0x08+t`, levels `+0x12+2t`, machine `+0x22+t`, machine pages `+0x2a+30t` / `+0x1da+30t`, AMP/LFO/FX page 1 `+0x11a+24t`, page 2 block `+0x2f2+30t`, slot record `+0x2ca+5t`, recorder setup `+0x602+12t`. Not carried by stock: scene locks (`+0x662+(s*8+t)*32`, per-scene bytes `+0x1662+10s+t`) and the LFO designer (`+0x1702+16t`, slope `+0x1782+2t`; MIDI `+0x1792+16m` / `+0x1812+2m`). MIDI slice: `+0x3e2+32m` (pages) and `+0x4e2+36m` (channel, bank, program). `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Applying Part data: `0x40001f18(bank, part, t)` publishes one track (engine state and memcpy, no kernel call); set the restart bit `0x8000184c` bit t first when the machine changed, as stock's machine edit `0x400973b4` does. The whole-Part apply `0x40009094` (1,492 B, parameters only) snaps in-flight slides on every track. At a pattern switch the engine runs the light apply `0x40009e00`: Part-wide bytes (the engine's bank / Part `0x80001828/29`, scene table, UI block) and, per track, only the LFO setup and only with LFO AUTO CHANGE (`0x80000050`) on; every other new setting reaches a voice at its next trig. `[emu]` (every byte compared)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Sequencer tick `0x400a1eea` (IPL 2): phase D `0x400a1f72`, E builds one step ahead (`0x400a2d7e` audio, `0x400a39c6` MIDI), F `0x400a3ca4`, G master `0x400a3f94`; master step `0x800065b2`, master tick `0x800065b6`; change gate `0x400a42fa`. The wrap body `0x400a43a0` commits a pending pattern whenever one is set and then runs the full switch, whose COND_RESET(-1) call is at `0x400a4850`. A:B pass counters `0x46107918[t]`. `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Stock switch timing (measured tick by tick): the new pattern's first step still runs at the outgoing master rate (`SCALE_IX` `0x8000663d` follows a step later); track reload counters stay 0 until the new pattern's first master wrap; MASTER_STEP reads 0 during the last audible step of the master cycle. An A:B pass starts at each track's own wrap (`0x400a536c`) and at the master restart, once when both coincide; FIRST trigs fire only in pass 1. `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Landing a track in phase: land one tick before the boundary with the first-fire bit (`0x80006624`) and reload `0x800065d3[t]` = tps - 2, and cancel the old boundary event a full tick ahead. Landing on the boundary tick itself left the old step in place now and then on the unit, because the sample clock and the old event's time are a frame apart there; the emulator's exact clock never showed it (I120, A70). Clocks: audio `0x4610757c` (127,008,000 a second; a tick at 120 BPM is `0x285ff0`, ~21 ms), MIDI `0x46107564` (a tick 16,800). The sequencer runs about a tick ahead of the audio; the engine places events 16 to a frame. `[hw]` (landing) / `[emu]` (values)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: SILENCE TRACKS is `0x8000004f` (setter `0x40065a96`, battery copy `0x100b14af`; per-track START SILENT at track record `+3`, -1 = the project's). At a pattern switch the engine hard-kills each silenced voice (`0x40006820`, from the loop at `0x4000d446`) instead of using the declicked note-off `0x40008f84(t)`. On stock a trig on the new pattern's step 0 restarts the voice in the same frame and hides the cut; a DIRECT JUMP landing mid-pattern popped on an MKI until the jump released the silenced tracks with the note-off a tick before the switch (V7.2.2, 2026-11-15, I119). Stock probably pops the same way when a ringing silenced track has no trig on step 0 (H32). `[hw]` (pop, fix) / `[emu]` (mechanism, ot_emu render)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Bank files on the card: chunk lengths are exact (error -51) and a 16-bit checksum covers every byte (-54), so there is no spare byte for mod data; keep it in a sidecar file in the project folder (Clyps' `clypsNN.work/.strd`, 2,568 B per bank, survived SAVE / RELOAD, EXPORT TO SET and DELETE PROJECT on an MKI with hooks at `0x400914de` and `0x4008ed5e`). Direct seek, checked on 816 real files (versions 0x14-0x17): PTRN n at `0x16 + st*n` (st = `0x8eec` from version 0x17, `0x8ee8` before), PART p at `0x16 + 16*st + 0x18bb*p`; OctaLib's table fits 0x17 only. A `.strd` holds 16 PTRN, 4 working PART and 4 SAVE PART chunks. Stock's buffered seek `0x4001660c` keeps a partly read buffer and the parser then finds no tag: seek the filesystem (`0x46c8243e`) to the block and drain the rest. `[doc]` / `[hw]` (sidecar)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Battery mirror: the UI bank's slabs are mirrored at `0x1001614e` (MIDI part `0x1001aa1e`), its Parts at `0x100a4ece`; that is what returns after a power cycle. Stock's `0x4000faf0` writes a whole bank (~620 KB) there; writing only changed records cut a one-track load from 36,568 to 2,466 B. `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Key layers: push `0x40031494`, pop `0x4003146c`, head `0x460d165c`; the last layer that lists a key wins (`-1` passes down, `0` swallows), but a key's sub-maps chain across layers (rebuild `0x4003125c`), so stock's FUNC sub-map `0x400bfa1e` still links above yours, and encoder records are copied as they are (no `-1` pass-down). A key held across a rebuild keeps its old handlers (`0x400312e2`). Copy T1's hold delay / repeat (`0x400bfc10`) into every key record you override: a key pressed under one layer and released under another with a different delay leaves its timer in the repeat list `0x460d1660`, and the UI task hangs at its next press. Held flags `0x46c7d8ee + code*24` ([FUNC] `0x2d` at `0x46c7dd26`); TRACK keys select on release; a double tap is a second press while `0x460d5de0` <= 14. Codes: UP `0x33`, DOWN `0x20`, LEFT `0x34`, RIGHT `0x21`, [PAGE] `0x1b`, [CUE] `0x2a`, PLAYBACK..FX2 `0x22..0x26`. `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Windows: `0x4005829c(w, h, dx, dy, prio, close_cb)` has five slots; opening priority P closes every window of priority >= P (toasts and SELECT 10, name editor 5, menus 3, project lists 2, Parts menu 1), and close_cb is never cleared. Window `+32` bit 0 is "visible" (the compositor `0x40013ad8` skips it), bit 5 "linked"; the manager finds a free slot by the linked bit, so hide a window by its visible bit, never by unlinking it (I121). Toast font `0x400ba862` (widths `0x400c205c`; a toast line holds 113 px), interface font `0x400ba876` (3x5 glyphs, 4 px advance, widths `0x400c246a`). `[hw]` / `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Track tabs and LEDs: three routines paint the main screen's track tabs on every UI pass, each with its own active-track test (`mvzb 0x80000000`): `0x4004bd48` (lower half), `0x4003fed8` (upper half) and `0x40044804` (a `!`-shaped status mark); they repaint only tabs whose cached state changed (side caches `0x400c0c50` / `0x400c0c94`). Redirecting fewer than all three gave half tabs and a stray `!` on a unit (I122). Trig LED buffer `0x460ba98c` (trig n = red die 2n, green 2n+1; stock dims to 7), LED layer table `0x460e7628`, push `0x4007e760`, pop `0x4007e81c`. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: `0x80000012` (MIDI tracks shown) is a long: a byte read gets its high byte, always 0; on a unit Clyps then showed and loaded audio tracks on the MIDI side, and RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT had the same read (I123). `0x80000000` is the active track of the side shown. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Probable stock gap: TRACK COPY `0x40029754` copies the record and six Part blocks but not the LFO designer, so a pasted track whose LFO uses the designer plays the destination's shape (SB26, not yet seen on a unit). The trigless-trig mask is read at track `+0x08` here, against `+0x10` on this page above (O32). `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: ColdFire build traps (KYOTI): a duplicate `.equ` lets the last one win without a warning (cost one flash round on a unit); hooks placed mid-function must save d0-d7/a0-a6 and replay the displaced instruction last, because stock branches on its flags; `-mcpu=5407` refuses cmpi to memory, `not.b`, `exg`, `cmpa.w`, movem with `-(sp)` / `(sp)+` and d16 offsets past 32767. The OS VERSION string holds 10 characters and the card `.bin` is ELUP-obfuscated, so check the name in the `.syx` (I124). `[hw]` / `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
text: Sample pool: KYOTI V1.8 (RELOAD + DIRECT JUMP) takes 11 pages, V1.8C and the CLYPS image 1,709 pages (~10 MB) of the 6 KB pages from the arena start `0x40a955e0`; the MEMORY page still reads 85.5 MB. A track-record copy (`0x40020898`) takes ~15-25 µs. `[doc]` {kyoti-1117}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
text: One-shot trig mask: byte 40 of an audio track record in the bank file (RAM: `bank + pattern*0x8ed8 + 31 + 0x91a*k`, i.e. track record `+0x1f`) is the low byte of the track's one-shot trig mask, bit 0 = step 1 ... bit 7 = step 8. With the step layout of the other masks (byte 7 - s/8) this puts the one-shot mask at `+0x18..0x1f` (inferred). A test project with no one-shots on steps 1-8 reads it as zero, which is how PATTERN MUTE mistook it for spare (I146, O32). `[hw]` (MKI over REMOTE) / `[emu]` {octabam-pmute-1118}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
text: Stock mute state: one per project, bits 8-15 of `0x80000008` for the audio tracks (FUNC+Tn toggles bit 8+n-1). The 22-byte state block at `0x80000000` is mirrored in battery RAM at `0x100b14cc` and restored at boot and by the new-project reset (`0x40025a90`); the power-up sanitiser is `0x4000fe20`. Byte `0x80000011` / `0x100b14dd` is referenced by nothing in the image (octabam uses bit 0 for its layer). A boot with empty battery RAM zeroes `0x100b14dc..df`; a boot with valid RAM writes nothing there. `[emu]` {octabam-pmute-1118}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
text: FUNC press: FUNC's press records sit at `0x400bfc12` (MKI) and `0x400c01f6` (MKII) key tables; its handler gets edge 1 on each press, and stock's double-press filter `0x40040250` (edge 3) does not run for FUNC. Panel parser row states `0x46100b18` (8 bytes): FUNC sets `0x20` of row 5, T2 `0x02` of row 2, trig 1 `0x01` of row 0 while held. Free-running timer DTCN3 `0xfc07c00c` (132 MHz). `[emu]` {octabam-pmute-1118}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
text: SAVE PROJECT path: PROJECT > SAVE is row action `0x40063890`; `0x400255ec` tests whether the project is on the card (if not: SAVE TO NEW `0x40063618`, name keyboard), then a YES/NO popup. YES `0x40063c54` stops the sequencer (`0x400a10c8`) and `0x40022850` posts a static record `{17, 0x400232bc, 0x40022e80, 0x40022dc4}` to the engine queue. Engine job 17 (`0x40085736`) opens the progress window via the sys task (event 43), runs the bank write `0x400919e4` and the project store `0x4008ee74` on the engine task, then `0x40022e80` closes the window with DONE! or stock's error text. 16 banks take over 6 s of emulated card time. `[emu]` {octabam-1118}

text: Stock delay routine cost: `0x400031a0` runs once a frame for all eight tracks, whatever their FX2 and however silent: 44.9 µs of the 362.8 µs frame (12.4 % of the ColdFire), stopped or playing. section: Syntakt / Recovery (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`)
text: Mod data written for defaults slows project load and save (Synfact, OS 1.41): a user saw a project load slowly when switched to from another project and save more slowly than usual; a reboot straight into it loaded normally. The export was valid. The ARP mod wrote and sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; leaving default carriers absent cut the emulated serialization from 24.8 M to 4.8 M instructions (81 % fewer). The slowness is a user report; the cost is `[emu]`, the wall-clock gain not yet measured. `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle} ([I50](../INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save))

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Stock public Machine IDs are 0-44, stored as a BYTE in each track's machine payload (`P[t]+0xA2`); runtime records `R[t] = model + 0x6C + 0x3C0*t`, `P[t] = *(R[t]+0x10)`; the setter is at `0x40025594` (store at `0x40025620`). 505 parameter descriptors of 52 bytes; only MAIN digital tracks 0-7. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Section 7 selector: a signed BYTE with a 46-entry map (negative -> 0, 0-45 kept, above 45 clamped to 45); stock maps 0-7 to the same-numbered engine family and 36->8, 37->9, 38->10, 44->11, everything else (incl. 45) to family 0. Stock tables: render pointers `0x400148F0` (12 entries), prep pointers `0x40014920`, the 46-byte map at `0x40014950`. A compact handoff moves MAIN `[0x80002000,0x800021B0)` through a 27x16-byte eDMA transfer (TCD47, channel 47); each track then receives a 20-byte copy into `T[t] = 0x80003C40 + 0x8E*t`. Dslot is 8 x `0x708` = 14,400 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Persistence confirmed statically: the current-kit Sound-v7 save/load keeps the machine byte (raw 0-45 and 255 retained, 46-254 map to 0); Pattern-v11 stores the byte at row `+0x2EC` and its restoration is not closed; Sound locks, p-locks, held trigs, migration, clipboard and undo not qualified. Evidence labels in that repo: confirmed by static analysis / verified in emulator (none for the whole device) / verified on hardware (none) / hypothesis. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: Signing conflict `[?]`: SyntHack describes an HMAC-SHA256 over the container for 1.41, with the key derived from the image. digikit found no HMAC trailer in 1.42 (the last 32 bytes are zero). Check the trailer of your own file before you decide.

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: Boot unpack limit: the bootstrap loads compressed section 3 at `0x40200000` and unpacks it to `0x40000400`. The margin (decompressed minus compressed) must stay below ~`0x1FFC00` at every point of the stream. Stock 1.41 has a margin of +99,938 B. A build padded with zeros to `0x40350000` (-8,751 B) did not boot, tested twice and hung on the logo. Zero padding is the worst case; already-compressed payloads raise the margin. SyntHack refuses builds under 4 KB of margin. `[hw]`

section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
text: Hardware lesson `[hw]`: SyntHack up to v0.8.0 kept mod code at `0x46000000`. Projects with SP TWINSHOT samples then crashed at boot. Since v0.8.1 the mod code (compressed, appended to section 3 at `0x40348000`) is unpacked into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. ([I20](../INCIDENTS.md#i20-mod-code-at-a-free-address-crashed-projects-with-certain-samples))

section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
text: Conflict to watch `[?]`: SY FM4 (OS 1.40A) copies its code to `0x47000000`, which it describes as "above the BSS end, below the stack, addressed by nothing". That is the region SyntHack found to be overwritten by sample loading on 1.41. Treat any use of RAM above the BSS as unsafe until it is tested with sample-heavy projects. Synfact's reading (2026-11-17) puts `0x47000000` inside the stock sample blob's span (`0x4584f2c5-0x4759b3c5` with all 64 slots full). `[emu]` {synfact-1118}

section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
text: Boot: entry `0x400004E8`; static constructors loop `0x40082500` (136 entries); the intro animation task `0x40087E6A` gates boot, so never make the intro longer. Screen: 128x64 1 bpp, column-major, double buffer at `0x402D6DC4`/`0x402D6DC0`; frame loop `0x4000A0E6` redraws when `*(0x444E1334)+96` is set. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: CPU #2 (section 7): all work runs in the audio interrupt `0x40000934` (vector 96, DMA timer 0 capture). Per block it copies `0x1B0` bytes of parameters from shared RAM and renders 8 digital voices (`0x40004324`). It returns 8 x 32 int32 over eDMA channel 47 and does no mixing. 12 engines: tables at `0x400148F0` (render), `0x40014920` (update), `0x40014950` (machine id -> engine). Order: BD MODERN, SD BASIC, CY ALLOY, PC CARBON, SY TONE, SY CHORD, SD VINTAGE, CP VINTAGE, SY TOY, SY BITS, SY SWARM, SP TWINSHOT. SY CHORD reads a 512 x int32 wave at `0x4001A300`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: CPU #1 (section 3): the per-block routine `0x400A3856` runs CV/gain, ADC deinterleave, then master/FX `0x4008F1CA`. Delay `0x40096890` and reverb `0x40096E3C` are the same code as on the Digitakt mk1. Buffers: digital tracks from CPU #2 at `0x80003D50`. ADC channels at `0x80003950`: 0-3 analog tracks, 4-5 external in, 6-7 the FX-track bus. USB/Overbridge: 20 channels per frame at `0x80004760`. The final mix is analog: digital buses go out through DACs into an analog mixer, with nothing digital after them. 40 control voltages go out over DSPI1 with eDMA channel 15; CV 35/36 are the FX-track bus VCAs. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: CPU #1 load: ~89 % at rest (sequencer stopped), measured on the device with DTIM0 (`0xFC07000C`) at interrupt entry and exit. The UI gets the rest, so a few thousand instructions per block make the UI lag. `[hw]` SY FM4 reports its main-CPU render at 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (stock 85.0k). That is a different span of the same interrupt. `[?]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: Digital filter and amp run on CPU #2; the cutoff is computed on CPU #1. Analog voices and the FX track drive a hardware envelope generator with 20-bit rate codes. Measured curves: the digital biquad f0 = 4.918 Hz x e^(0.0655 x FREQ); the analog filter f = 14.645 Hz x e^(0.0574 x FREQ). Tempo is at `0x402D7010` (BPM x 120). `[hw]` (analog curves measured)

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Section 7 is byte-identical in 1.41 and 1.42 (SHA-256 `daf6451c...783bc2`). It is ColdFire ISA-C with EMAC, MCF5441x-class: compile with `-mcpu=54418`, disassemble with `-m m68k:isa-c:emac`. CPU #2 has its own 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000` (SP `0x48000000`, entry `0x40001070`). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Only 39.8 KB is code (`0x40000404-0x40009f88`: boot, audio interrupt, voice loop, 12 engines, sample loader), followed by 284 KB of tables and data. Code room for mods is almost nil: ~318 bytes in small pieces remained after SynCrackd's images.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: CPU #2 configures its own FPGA: a packed bitstream at `0x40041060` is unpacked to `0x40042000` (54,664 bytes) at init. That is the same size as the Analog Heat +FX FPGA section, so it may be the same part `[?]`. Keep away from it (rule A22).

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: The sample pool is in CPU #2's RAM: 64 MB from `0x4004f750`, in BSS zeroed at boot. A 64-entry slot table `{u32 frames, u32 pointer}` is at `0x4404f754`. Format: 64 times `u32 frames` + big-endian int16 mono. The main CPU fills it at boot in 2 KB chunks through the shared window `0x800`, with an unchecked 16-bit index. This is the slow boot the manual mentions. Per slot at most 524,287 frames (10.9 s; positions are 20.12 fixed point). The stock UI limits slots to 5 s and "32 MB".

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Above the BSS, `0x4404f980-0x48000000` (63.7 MB) is not referenced by any section-7 instruction and is used for SynCrackd's state. Leave the top megabyte for the stack (its depth is not measured). This is CPU #2's RAM, not the main CPU's region that sample loading overwrites (CONFLICTS O2). `[hw]` (alpha, one unit)

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Shared window (CPU #2 `0x0-0x1000` = main CPU `0x10000000`, chip select 0, 16-bit, one wait state): `0x000-0x1b0`: the parameter block, copied to `0x80008000` every block; `0x1b0-0x5b0`: 8 mono track buffers, sent by eDMA 47; `0x5b0-0x800`: unused by stock; `0x800-0x1000`: the sample chunk at boot.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: SRAM `0x80000000`: 8 voices of 1,800 B, 8 mono int32 output buffers, 8 parameter blocks of 142 B. The highest static reference is `0x8000f670`, so treat SRAM as full.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Twinshot (engine 11, machine type 44) reads the parameter slots 18-25: TUN1, SMP1, FLT1, MIX, TUN2, SMP2, loop flag, DEC1. A sample select below the centre plays the slot in reverse. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: SynCrackd replaces Twinshot (and CY ALLOY) with a 64-slot stereo sampler, loops, slices, time stretch and transient triggers. It is OS 1.42 only, alpha, tested in emulation and on one unit, MIT.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Synfact (OS 1.41; source builds on 1.42 from core 2.0, 2026-11-17) adds DT mk1 sample machines, a per-project pool, polyphony across tracks and a third LFO. It ships its firmware change as a zlib-compressed XOR mask against the official file, pinned by hash. It needs a second mods file (515,808 B) sent with its own transfer tool after the flash. Boot is confirmed on a unit (core 1.4 and 1.7.2, 2026-11-09); the safe-boot rollback is not yet tested on hardware. `[hw]` {synfact} {synfact-core}

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Each change is stored with the SHA-256 of the original bytes, so a different OS version fails the build instead of crashing. Every mod runs in a Unicorn emulator next to the original code before flashing. Stock Unicorn gets signed fractional EMAC wrong (the audio comes out silent), so EMAC instructions are trapped and executed in Python from the NXP manual. Use CPU model "ANY" (the code needs FF1, MVS/MVZ, SATS).

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Hooks: replace at least 6 bytes with `jsr` plus `nop` padding, and the trampoline replays the replaced instructions. Save every register; replay replaced EMAC instructions first. If your code uses EMAC, set MACSR yourself and leave ACC0 at 0, because the OS sum routines start from it. One-time setup goes in a hook in the page initializer (`0x401885D2...`), never in boot time.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Mod code: gcc/as with `-mcpu=54418`, no `.bss` (put variables in `.data`), no libgcc (`nm -u` empty). ColdFire limits: `muls.l` takes no absolute address, there is no `exg`, `movem` takes only `(An)`/`d16(An)`, short branches reach ±127 B.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Spare storage the OS saves without knowing: per track: engine word +106 (hidden id 72); per kit: unused words of the pattern kit at `*0x800030BC` (ids 0, 0x1A, 0x24, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x37, 0x46, 0x38). Store values XOR their default, so old projects load with defaults; kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track kit blocks (Digitakt MIDI-track data, unused here); 256 bytes in the project settings file. A "free" parameter id can be an alias the OS shows in some modes, so audit it.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: UI internals: parameter descriptors at `0x4022D59C + 52*id`; page objects at `0x41B9F3C8` (44 B, 8 slots); per-parameter `std::function` objects at `0x41B9FA24 + 84*id` (+20 text, +36 icon, +68 style). Page 25 ("OB8") is a free Digitakt leftover. Rewrite a `std::function` only from UI code, never from the audio interrupt.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Audio mods: Hook the mix function; keep the OS's EMAC `msac` sign convention (the result is -Σ g·x). Do nothing when there is nothing to do. Compute at 24 kHz where the sound allows it. Ramps must snap to their target or the effect never goes idle. Limit how far a modulated delay moves per block. Keep a cost-per-block regression test (count instructions with `UC_HOOK_CODE` after `ctl_flush_tb()`).

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Where mod code lives at run time (SyntHack modarea, v0.8.1+): The OS image has only ~2 KB free, and everything after it is zeroed at boot. So mod code is appended to section 3 compressed (SHLZ, at `0x40348000 + offset`). At boot it is unpacked into the first 64 KB block of the OS heap: buddy allocator `0x4010350C`, 16 MB pool at `0x444E38C0`. The block is reserved by a call right after heap initialization, so it always gets index 0, and the OS never hands it out again. The earlier home above the BSS (`0x46000000`) was overwritten whenever samples loaded (SyntHack issue 4), which settles conflict O2. `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Kit and project storage that round-trips through stock code (SyntHack kitstore/projstore): Kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track blocks go into 6 file bytes that stock's writer zeroes and its reader ignores. 256 bytes go into the project settings block (`+0x227..+0x3FF` is zeroed by the writer and ignored by the reader), behind an `SH` marker. Tests run the real writer and reader with and without the hooks. Zero must mean "default", because stock-saved files load as zero. `[emu]` {synthack-mods}

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Controlling the analog side digitally (SyntHack master-comp): a feed-forward compressor detects on ADC 6/7 (the FX-track bus before its VCAs) and applies gain through those VCAs' control voltages (CV 35/36), once per block (~1.5 kHz). Its UI uses the Digitakt MIDI-track "CC Select" ids 262-268, which the Syntakt never uses. Cost: ~100 instructions per block when off, ~600 when on. Checked on the device (v0.9). `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Projects: SyntHack OS (9 mods on hardware, MIT); SY FM4 (4-operator FM replacing SY TONE, which also patches CPU #2); Syntakt Firmware Workbench. The Workbench replaces SY CHORD's waves: 31 slots of 257 big-endian Q31 samples, measured on a unit within 1 %. It adds a Deja Vu LFO, DV-H. It refuses any file but 1.41 and checks that only the declared regions changed. `[hw]` {syntakt-workbench}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
text: `Syntakt_OS1.42.syx`: ELE3, 2,029,486 bytes, META stamp 2026-09-30 (same day as DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12), SHA-256 `ded3c59f...7f37c1`; SysEx transport id `0x16`, OS-stream byte `0x11`; same packing codec as DT2/DN2; per-packet checksum constant K = 0x11. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
text: No HMAC trailer - the Syntakt OS file is not signed (no SHA-256 constants in sections 2-4); only the content checksum applies. `[doc]` {digikit-f70} Correction 2026-11-18: there is no trailer slot at all; the container (2,029,392 bytes, the value in its length word) ends at the end of section 8 rounded up to 16, where DT2/DN2 add 32 bytes, and digikit's rebuild of the stock file matches it byte for byte. `[doc]` {digikit-st-1118}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
text: Sections: 5 META; 2 bootstrap (dest word `0x04000000`, ColdFire code at `0x8000xxxx`, 30,782 B); 1 present only on Syntakt: `0xFF` padding then a bitstream-like blob (149,516 B) - the FPGA configuration (the bootstrap configures a Xilinx-style FPGA via INIT_B/DONE; MAIN only reads a status word); 3 MAIN at `0x40000400` (3,442,576 B, same reset path as DT2: entry `0x400004e8`, SP `0x48000000`); 4 UPDATER at `0x80000400` (32,768 raw); 6 present only on Syntakt (1,744 B; per digikit's newer reading the peer CPU's stage-1 loader, linked at SRAM `0x80000000` {digikit-st-1118}); 7 is not a SHARC stream here but a standalone ColdFire program linked at `0x40000400` (entry `0x40001070`, 383,760 B) driving a DSPI-like block at `0xFC05C000` - consistent with a second ColdFire that runs the digital machines `[?]`; 8 byte-identical to DT2/DN2's section 8. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`

Peer states include LOAD_OS, BOOT, RUNNING, UPLOAD_SAMPLES. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
text: The analog tracks reuse the Analog Rytm MKII's voice design. The voice control records have the Rytm MKII's format (command/depth word, start and target bytes, mode nibble, rate exponent and mantissa). The cymbal oscillator banks use the Rytm's scale (43.62 units per Hz) and load the Rytm's CH/CB CLASSIC values. So Rytm voice research applies here and back. `[doc]` (inferred from the shared formats)

section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
text: Digital tracks: rendered on CPU #2, then handed over by mailbox and eDMA channel 47 to CPU #1, which mixes them and sends them to the SSI1 codec. This agrees with SyntHack's audio path above. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
text: An emulator now boots 1.42 with both CPUs (analog-emu: stage 1 the main screen with a stand-in for CPU #2, stage 2 CPU #2 running for real). It is the only Syntakt 1.42 emulator in the catalogue; SyntHack's Unicorn harness targets 1.41. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Bank store: two 8 MiB slots inside the old 16 MiB `/mods` reservation, metadata sectors at eMMC `0x02bffe00` and `0x033ffe00`; the legacy record at `0x03400000` is still read. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Safe boot: a bank moves CANDIDATE -> TRYING (written before any bank code runs) -> GOOD, set once AUDIO and the sample pool are ready and 150 UI ticks (about 5 s) have passed; a crash or power-off before that boots the previous GOOD bank or stock machines. Each bank names an exact core contract, and the core checks the stock bytes that LFO3 and MODULATION SKIP patch before any initializer runs. `[doc]`, rollback `[?]` (not yet tested on hardware). The first trial crashed every boot (I62).

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Filter table: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from `0x40040060` (508 poles, then a zero tail; indices up to 1023 are read). A mod window in that tail made BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles; core 1.7.2 bounds the index. `[hw]` (I63)

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Load: MAIN is about 88 % with a plain pattern and 91-92 % with three POLY voices; code fetched from DDR costs far more than its instruction count (I64). `[hw]` {synfact-chorus}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Load after the MAIN optimisation (owner's unit, OS 1.41, stock pattern, 2026-11-13/14): a minimal bank (System Info + Modulation Skip) reads 81 % MAIN, the full bank 86 % before and 83 % after the optimisation release; about 2 points sat in LFO3's per-block callback, about 1 in the stereo audio callbacks. The meter rounds to whole percent; at 48 kHz and 32-sample blocks one MAIN point is about 6.7 µs per block. `[hw]` {synfact-main-opt}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Appended boot storage is wiped at startup: on OS 1.41 the storage appended after the MAIN image is cleared and reused once the early resident copy is done, so code placed there is gone when the application runs; only the resident reserve (64 KiB in Synfact's core) is safe for code called after boot (I104). `[hw]` {synfact-main-opt}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Stock track types: every stock digital track type has bit 6 clear; Synfact's machines use types 64-79, so a mod can tell that all tracks are stock from the type bytes alone. The MAIN audio interrupt calls the stock modulation routine `0x40097afc` for every track on every block (about 6,600 emulated instructions for the full body). `[doc]` / `[emu]` {synfact-main-opt}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Build and voices: builds use `-mcpu=54415` (an MCF5441x part), SMZ bank code `-fno-jump-tables`. Each track has one stock voice block at `0x80000000 + t*0x708`; the stock voice reset rewrites +`0x570`-`0x708` and zeroes 48 bytes at the pointer in +`0x56c`. `[doc]` {synfact-machine-ref}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Free memory, checked on a unit (2026-11-10): a probe machine (type 70, MEM PROBE) filled the shared-window gap `0x5b0..0x7df` (AUDIO `0x5b0`, MAIN `0x100005b0`) and the AUDIO SRAM tail `0x8000f398..0x8000ffff` (after FM TONE's scratch; the stock boot leaves it zero) with a pattern and checked it every block: nothing else wrote either area over several minutes. Synfact core 1.8 uses both for stereo tracks. `[hw]` {synfact-memprobe}

section: Syntakt / SY SWARM read from the audio program (model27 notes/84, OS 1.42 section 7, same in 1.41, 2026-11-16)
text: Engine 10 (SY SWARM): update `0x400092ec`, render `0x400096e8`. Seven sawtooths from band-limited tables, one per octave (`0x40006588` picks the table by note, `0x40006434` reads it with linear interpolation); a centre that SUB moves down 0, 1 or 2 octaves (its increment shifted right and its table picked again, nothing else), six detuned oscillators driven by six tables indexed by DET; ANIM is three slow sines (about 1, 2 and 5 Hz, `0x40006074`) that phase-modulate oscillator pairs in opposite directions; NMOD is a noise generator (`0x40003eb4`) that phase-modulates the six; MIX uses two gain tables; every oscillator gets a random phase at a trig. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / SY SWARM read from the audio program (model27 notes/84, OS 1.42 section 7, same in 1.41, 2026-11-16)
text: Its six detune tables equal Adam Szabo's published Super Saw model (his offsets times his 11th-degree detune polynomial, KTH 2010) to 0.000 cents over all 128 × 6 values; its mix curves are not his. `[doc]` (computed by model27, static reading)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Sequencer step per track (MAIN): the sequencer runs in a forced interrupt at `0x4008c924` (24 ticks a quarter note) for 13 tracks (12 = FX). Per track `t`: next step `0x43bd73fc+t`, step before `0x43bd7416+t`, ticks into the step `0x43bd7409+t`, steps toward the bar `0x43bd753c+t`. The step advances at `0x4008d0e4..0x4008d120`; length is the track's (track record `+969`, a word; record = pattern + `0x499*t`) when pattern byte `+0x21379` is set, else the pattern's (`+0x21374`). Trig preparation `0x4008b882` at tick 0 (call sites `0x4008cf00`, `0x4008cf14`; `0x4008c204` for a pattern started mid-way). UI copies `0x444e2370+t` (last) and `0x444e237d+t` (step), copied each tick at `0x4008d1a8`; live recording reads `0x444e2370`. `[doc]` / `[emu]` (Unicorn)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: View manager (UI controller +`0x40`): list sentinel +`0x14`, tail +`0x18`, highest opaque node +`0x1c`; a node holds its view at +`0x8`; a view's closed flag is a byte at +`0x30`. Native close `0x400ffd02` sets it and requests deferred cleanup (manager +`0x22`); it does not destroy the view, and a shared owner can keep it alive after removal. Push `0x40100bc2` calls visibility `0x40100ade` before the new view's attach callback; visibility composes the UI synchronously (`0x4000a0e6`) and runs mod tick code. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Stock deferred cleanup drops a close raised during composition: cleanup `0x40100ea4` clears manager +`0x22` at `0x40100f2c..0x40100f3e` after the visibility call, so a close requested by a tick inside that call is lost and the closed view stays in the list (key walks skip it but nothing removes it). Synfact core 1.8.2 moves the clear before the call. Mods that close views from tick code are exposed. `[emu]` (reproduced; the related unit symptom is I115)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)

The tail `0x4008fb38` combines ADC `0x8000ded0` with the preview bus `0x8000dfd0` and runs USB and codec output; six 256-byte buses start at `0x8000dad0`. Native transport STOP is `0x4008c288`. `[emu]` (analog-emu interpreter)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: Stock builds one sample blob in MAIN DDR at boot: the native builder (`0x400822bc` on 1.41, `0x40082334` on 1.42) reads each of the 64 stock slots through a temporary 512 KiB buffer and concatenates them at physical `0x4584f2c5` (used through the uncached alias `0x4d84f2c5`; same address on both OS versions): 64 `u32` frame counts, then 2 bytes per mono frame, no 64-byte SAMP header; an empty slot still takes its 4-byte count. With 64 five-second slots it is 30,720,256 bytes (29.30 MiB) and ends at `0x4759b3c5` (exclusive). The stock sender (`0x40082f90` on 1.42) then copies it in 2,048-byte pages through the mailbox at `0x10000800`; CPU #2 keeps its own copy. `[emu]` (Unicorn running each OS's own builder with file and heap stand-ins)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: So `0x45565490-0x48000000` is unsafe from about `0x4584f2c5` up: past 8,064,315 bytes of blob (84.000625 s of mono 48 kHz PCM16 in all, for example 17 five-second samples) it reaches `0x46000000`; in the reproduction the first overlapping write came from stock's memcpy (`0x40115f94` on 1.41, `0x40116158` on 1.42) while copying slot 17. This is the mechanism behind SyntHack's lesson at `0x46000000` (I20) and also covers SY FM4's `0x47000000`. Limiting each slot to 5 s does not keep it out. `[emu]` / `[hw]` (I145)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: CPU #2 reads the stock pool at `0x4004f750`: its receiver (`0x40000fba`) and descriptor parser (`0x40000d06`) use that base, unchanged from 1.41 to 1.42 (section 7 is identical). Synfact's 1.42 port first moved the base to `0x4004f7c8` by mistake; core 2.0.1 restores it. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: Stock per-slot limit as Synfact checks it: one sector per stock header, a SAMP header and at most 240,000 mono frames (5 s); a slot's on-disk body is at most 480,064 bytes (64-byte header plus PCM). All 64 full slots are 15,001 sender pages. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: Synfact core 2.0.1 streams instead: it no longer calls the stock builder; it plans the 64 slots from their headers and builds each sender page on demand from eMMC (byte-identical to the old blob), using 5,120 bytes of MAIN scratch freed by a task-only hook at `0x40083026` after the last mailbox copy. Waveform envelopes are read lazily (at most 4,096 PCM bytes per UI idle call); the cache is about 98 KiB for 128 entries, allocated on first use. The native heap is 16 MiB, too small for a 29.3 MiB blob anyway. Resident use: 65,116 of 65,536 bytes (420 free). `[emu]` (sender, page and parser code run in Unicorn); boot with 64 five-second samples `[hw]` (prototype, owner's unit)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: OS 1.42 versus 1.41 (MAIN): build id 0097 (1.41: 0094); MAIN decoded 3,442,576 bytes (3,438,480); container 2,029,392 bytes (2,028,880), plus 94 transport-padding bytes in the .syx; SRAM copy source end `0x40348b90` (`0x40347b90`); BSS clear end `0x45566490` (`0x45565490`); boot stack `0x48000000` on both. MAIN SHA-256 `1a9723b1...eb3e7`. Sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8 (bootstrap, updater and AUDIO included) are byte-identical; section 5 and the container header change. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: No single offset from 1.41 to 1.42: code and tables moved by `+0x78`, `+0xac`, `+0x1c4`, `+0x29c`, `+0x2a0`, `+0x320` or `+0x354`; the DDR image and BSS by `+0x1000`. Synfact found its 108 sites with masked byte-pattern contexts and then checked each one. Examples (1.41 -> 1.42): draw-all `0x401007ce` -> `0x40100992`; operator new `0x40103788` -> `0x4010394c`; menu item ctor `0x400fa688` -> `0x400fa84c`; menu add `0x400f9ebe` -> `0x400fa082`; app startup site `0x400826a6` -> `0x4008271e`; mixer call `0x400a4fce` -> `0x400a5046` (calls `0x4008f1ca` -> `0x4008f242`); modulation `0x40097afc` -> `0x40097b74`; LFO `0x40119266` -> `0x4011942a`; deferred view cleanup's clear `0x40100f2c` -> `0x401010f0`; trig preparation `0x4008b882` -> `0x4008b8fa`. Key and encoder dispatch (`0x4000839e`, `0x400083f0`) and the vector-base routine `0x40001d28` did not move. `[doc]` (G5 anchor data)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: How the peer CPU gets its program: MAIN reads ids 6 and 7 from the OS directory in NOR (`0x80000`, "ELE3", 16-byte entries from `0x80020`: id, offset, length) and streams them at every boot over DSPI2 (`0xEC038000`) in slave mode, eDMA channel 29 one byte per request. Buffers are `0xAA | big-endian length | payload`: id 6 at `0x4f8af2c1` after eight `0xFF` bytes (MAIN changes byte 1 from `0x01` to `0x0f`), id 7 at `0x4f84f2c1` (length limit `0x5fffb`, matching SY FM4's "0x60000 - 5"). Section 6 (stage 1, SRAM `0x80000000`) sets up DDR, takes the stream and jumps through `*(0x40000400)`. Who starts DSPI0 as master before stage 1 is open. `[doc]` (stream bytes `[emu]`: payload equals section 7 by SHA-256)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Two pins form the handshake: MAIN's doorbell (GPIO port A bit 4) is the peer's DTIM0 capture event (vector 96); the peer's pin (port 6 bit 2: set via `0xEC09401E`, cleared via `0xEC09402A`) is MAIN's EPORT IRQ4 (vector 68). Peer steps the window state `+8` from 1 to `0xC` (hello "HO"/"HA" at `+0/+2`, `0xA5A5` at `+4`, window RAM test with `0xAAAAAAAA`/`0x55555555`, sample chunks), then installs its frame handler `0x40000934`. MAIN status `0x41bbf448` and state `0x41bb32b0` reach 6. Without a peer, "DSP BOOT FAILURE (TIMEOUT)" follows after `0x12` poll periods (about 1.04 G emulated instructions). `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: MAIN mixes the digital voices and owns the audio clock: eDMA ch 54 (TCD `0xFC0456C0`) streams a 2 KB ring at SRAM `0x80000000` (64 frames x 8 words) to the SSI TX FIFO `0xFC0C8000`; its half-way interrupt is the 1500 Hz audio frame (32 samples at 48 kHz, SSI1 slave; vector 174, handler `0x400a2058`). That handler forces INTC1 source 63 to run the engine tick (vector 191, `0x400a38ce`, 7,550 bytes), which mixes the 8 voices from `0x80003d50` in Q31 and fills the other half. Main L/R sit in ring words 5 and 3 as 24-bit signed (the Q31 mix shifted right by 8). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Frame budget numbers (emulator): MAIN needs about 117,000 instructions per frame; the peer's frame handler about 86,500 idle and up to 88,900 with a note. digikit runs MAIN at 189.9 M instructions/s (264 MHz core over a measured busy CPI of 1.39); at one instruction per 132 MHz bus tick (88,000 per frame) MAIN did not fit. The peer's hottest code is the voice oscillator `0x4000290e` (98 instructions, 18 call sites, 21-24 % of the frame handler). `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Profiling clock: stock MAIN reads DTIM2's counter DTCN2 (`0xFC07800C`, started by the boot loader; MAIN never writes `0xFC078000-0xFC07800F`) and busy-waits on it; DT2/DN2 use DTIM0. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: MAIN RAM map 1.42: reset path clears `0x4033a000..0x45566490` (bss end); nothing above. Heap: buddy allocator `0x401036d0` (free `0x401038d6`), descriptor `0x402d5324`, 16 MiB at `0x444e48c0..0x454e48c0` (1.41: `0x444E38C0`). DMA data through the `+0x08000000` alias: slots `0x45570000..0x45609000`, `0x45608000..0x4564f0a0`, eMMC bounce buffers `0x4582f080..0x4583f280`, the sample stage buffer from `0x4584f2c0`, the section-7 transmit buffer `0x4784f2c1..0x478af2cb`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: The top 4 MiB of DDR is a ring: `0x400966e0` memsets 4 MiB at uncached `0x4fc00000` at boot; `0x4009687a` and `0x4009748c` index it as `0x4fc00000 + 8*(i & 0x7ffff)`, advance by `0x20` per frame and hand it to eDMA. So cached `0x47c00000..0x48000000` is cleared at every boot and written every frame (that it is the delay memory is open; SyntHack called `0x4FC00000` delay/reverb lines on 1.41). digikit's first `cf.expansion` (`0x47e8b000..0x47fe0000`) sat inside it and was moved. `[doc]` (O35)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Why SyntHack's `0x46000000` code got overwritten (inferred): MAIN builds the 64 sample slots for upload at `0x4584f2c0` (`0x40082334`), and the section-7 buffer starts 32 MB later at `0x4784f2c1`; `0x46000000` and SY FM4's `0x47000000` fall in that stage buffer, and the stock UI's "32 MB" sample limit matches its size. `[?]` (ties to I20, I145)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: digikit's proposed mod RAM on 1.42 (not canary-tested): `cf.expansion` `0x478c0000..0x47bf0000` (3.2 MiB, 64 KiB above the section-7 buffer, 64 KiB below the ring), keep area `0x47bf0000..0x47bf1000`, flash cave `0x40339730..0x4033a000` (2,256 zero bytes after the 136-entry init table; 1.41's cave was `0x40338740..0x40339000`). A 31 MiB unreferenced gap `0x458b0000..0x4784f2c1` is deliberately not used. `[doc]` (boot `[emu]`)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Board facts same as DT2/DN2: UART8 `0xEC070000` (same init and TX code), eSDHC `0xFC0CC000` (same driver, same 4-part eMMC whitelist at `0x402d5b40`), DDR 128 MiB at `0x40000000` (bootstrap SDRAM setup byte-identical; CACR `0xa50ce100`, ACR0 `0x4007e020`), soft reset `0x400058f4` (drain UART, `clr.l 0x48000000`, `0x80` to `0xEC090000`). Which eMMC part a real Syntakt carries is open. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Card layout 1.42 (512-byte sectors, MmcFs only, no path filesystem): header at 0 (magic `0xBEEFBACE`); write-protect bitmaps at `0x800` (272 B, no kit bitmap); 2,048 sound slots of 2 sectors at `0x1000`; 64 sample slots ("SAMP", `0x400` sectors) at `0x2000..0x12000`; two "COKi" arena copies at `0x7a000`/`0x7c000`; working project at `0x7e000`; 128 project slots of 4 MiB at `0x80000..0x180000`. MmcFs writes refuse sector >= `0x180000`. An emulated session (save project, save sound, format +Drive) wrote at most sector `0x81f7f` and erased up to `0x17ffff`. `[doc]`/`[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Host-controlled card offsets (stock, all three devices): the MidiRpc Read/Write/Clear/Copy/Move/Swap handler (`0x4010bd9a`) writes the card through `SafeMmcStreamWriter` at the offset the host sends; nothing bounds it except the card capacity. A host that sends a mod store's offset erases it. digikit lists bounding this as its first open item before any hardware use. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: PCB revision byte and the "TOO OLD HARDWARE" screen: MAIN maps FlexBus CS1 at address 0 (128 KiB, read only) and reads a revision byte there (letter = bits 0-4, number - 1 = bits 5-7, self-test prints `PCBA0046%c%d`). Below letter D the boot shows "TOO OLD HARDWARE FOR THIS OS"; `0x23`, `0x43`, `0x82` give "WILL NOT BE COMPATIBLE"; `0x4008248c` takes a newer-board path from letter E. CS0 is the 128 KiB peer window at `0x10000000`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Analog calibration record (factory data): SPI NOR `0x300000`, `0x22d40` bytes, magic "RBOZ" (`0x52424f5a`), checksum at `+0xc` (sum of `i ^ byte`), u16 `+0x10 == 1`, eight marker bytes non-zero; a backup copy is read from NOR `0x340000`. Invalid -> "RUN WARM-UP CALIBRATION" at boot. Writers: `0x4006eb7e` (calibration menu), self-test `0x40080646`. Same family as the A4's "RBOW" at `0x300000`. Never write it. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: NOR driver: DSPI `0xFC05C000` with a GPIO chip select (port 6 bit 4, `0x40114288`); pages `0x100`, sectors `0x10000`, erase in `0x40000` blocks; program `0x40117a72`, erase `0x40117aee`/`0x40117b58`. The OS writer `0x4011aad4` ("Writing Flash") erases and writes from NOR `0x80000`. Self-test also erases `0x3c0000`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Run-time windows MAIN drives (digikit's `[protect]` list): `0x0-0x1FFFF` (CS1), `0x10000000-0x1001FFFF` (peer link), FlexBus regs `0xFC008000`, DSPI `0xFC05C000` (NOR), DSPI1 `0xFC03C000` (per audio block a `0x830`-byte eDMA frame on ch 15 plus PCS1 register writes, and the boot FPGA load `0x400bcb4e`), DSPI2 `0xEC038000`, GPIO `0xEC094000-0xEC0940FF` (FPGA INIT `0xEC09401C` bit 0, DONE `0xEC09401D` bit 7). No MAIN writer of analog voice hardware was found. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Panel wire and firmware key index differ: wire code = channel*8 + bit + 1 (1-48, 49 = channel 6 bit 0, LEVEL push). Codes: 1-16 trigs, 17 FUNC, 18 TRK, 19 TRIG, 20 SYN, 21 none, 22 FLTR, 23 AMP, 24 LFO, 25 SETTINGS, 26 FX, 27 TEMPO, 28 NO, 29-31 LEFT/DOWN/RIGHT, 32 PAGE, 33 BANK, 34 PTN, 35 SONG/SOUND (three dots), 36 REC, 37 PLAY, 38 STOP, 39 YES, 40 UP, 41-48 encoder pushes G,F,E,B,A,D,C,H. The decoder `0x40103094` maps wire to key index through `0x401d7a48`, and `key_down` (`0x40102f40`) maps back through `0x401d7984`: trig keys 1-16 are firmware key indices 24-39 (on DT2/DN2 both tables are the identity). MAIN has no boot-time key reader. `[emu]` (sweep) / `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: LED protocol (44 RGB LEDs): not the DT2/DN2 `b9 idx val`. `b5 n r g b` sets palette entry n (41 entries, 5 bits per channel); `b0..b3 led n` assigns a palette entry to LED state 0-3; `0x20+k, v` sets LEDs 4k..4k+3 at two bits each (3 = idle). LEDs 0-15 trigs, 18-22 page keys (radio group), 36 REC, 37 PLAY, 40-43 pattern pages. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Peer facts not on this page yet: section 7 zeroes `0x4004f6e0..0x4404f980` and builds a 256-entry vector table at `0x4004005c`; per frame its eDMA ch 47 (TCD `0xFC0455E0`) sends 1 KB to window `+0x1b0`. Section 8 is an NXP i.MX RT image (IVT at `0x1000`, entry `0x60042000`). Forum photos: two Spartan-3A (XC3S200A), DDR2 Nanya NT5TU128M8HE. `[doc]`/`[?]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: 1.42 addresses resolved by unique hash (semantics `[?]`): task_create `0x40001640`, sem_pend `0x40001792`, sleep_us `0x401162f8`, main OS task site `0x4000abd6`, UI loop `0x4000b2d8`, idle site `0x40082896`, MIDI rx `0x40103f5e`, MIDI send `0x40106728`, block read/write `0x4010f612`/`0x4010f7f8`, SETTINGS list tail `0x4005f176`, toast `0x400c347c`, reset init calls `0x4000053e` (stock bytes `4eba ff1c 4eba ff6e`). section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Run the emulator before every flash; the unit should only judge sound and feel.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Test what the hardware actually consumes (the frames the CPU sends and the DSP's output). Never test by reading back what your patch wrote.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Exercise the real path (sequencer, several tracks, a track other than 1) and the extremes: hard pan, 0 and 127, maximum feedback, every machine, unison.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Check any stock state you read on every variant (every machine and filter type).

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: If a gesture works on stock pages but not on yours, find the stock routine and its bound (Digitone II: `slot <= 100`).

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Keep levels honest: measure worst cases, report them, avoid unrequested gain compensation; send-FX returns are wet only; clamp every audio-writing build; never read memory you did not write.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Profile L2/DDR accesses; if the unit's load disagrees with the emulator, measure on the unit before optimising. Keep per-block CPU work small, defer per-note work.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Do not call a root cause certain until the hardware agrees.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)
text: Never overwrite the stock image. Know the source of any third-party download.

section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Rules (each from a hardware round trip)

The DT2 engine scales with what plays and governs its own load: with 8 heavy tracks it ran at 99-100 % for whole windows and missed no block. Budgets measured on one device say nothing about the other. {dn2-sharcload} {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices

These are not the same experiment (sustained overload by added voices vs. single late blocks), so they do not contradict each other. A test that settles it: provoke single late blocks on a DN2 the way the DT2 test did. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2mk2-reports}

text: Bricking is usually recoverable when the bootloader is untouched; the danger is projects that modify boot code or lack a documented recovery path. Subtle DSP/bus timing bugs are more likely to ruin a session than bricking. One mod developer bricked an Akai MPC Sample in September (video). section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
text: The Digitone II 1.11 example file has 18,668 SysEx messages, 8-in-7 encoding, per-packet checksums, a container with model/version/overall checksum and an HMAC-SHA256 signature the tool recomputes on repack. Section 3 (MAIN OS) is the usual target; leave 2 (bootstrap) and 4 (updater) alone because the bootloader holds the recovery menu; section 8 appears as `?` (no known name); section IDs differ on other devices, so `-i` is authoritative. `.raw` sections are copied as-is, `.bin` sections are decompressed. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
text: Editing rules: overwrite bytes only, the file size must not change (later addresses shift); replacement text must be the same length and use characters already present; keep the terminating zero byte; always edit a copy in `work/` and keep `extracted/` untouched; verify with `cmp -l` (exactly the intended number of changed bytes) and by re-extracting section 3 from the new file and comparing it byte-for-byte; `-V` must not exceed the original version string length (e.g. 4 characters like `1.11`). The repacked file is smaller than Elektron's because the tool compresses slightly better (level 3 took ~14 s, level 0 is ~18x faster and ~3 % larger). The author states the worked example (replacing "UNTITLED" with "ELEKMODS") was not tested on hardware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Digitakt II: section 2 = bootstrap, section 4 = updater (never modify); the DSP program is an ADI boot stream in section 7; ElekLabs digikit's patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8.

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Section 7 is a stream of ADI boot records (the ADSP-2156x hardware reference, boot chapter). Each header is four little-endian uint32s: block code, target, byte count, argument. The block code's top byte is `0xad`; its byte at offset 2 makes the XOR of all 16 header bytes zero; its low 16 bits are flags: `0x0001` LOAD (copy `count` bytes to the target), `0x0101` FILL (fill with the argument), `0x5001` FIRST + IGNORE (starts a boot image; target = entry in PC16, argument = distance from the end of this header to the next FIRST), `0x0801` INIT and `0x8001` FINAL (end the image and the stream). Later loads overwrite earlier ones in order, and stock relies on that (15 overlapping loads and fills on DN2 1.12). To add code, insert records before FINAL and grow only the last FIRST's argument and XOR byte; dt2-machine-lab used FILL records to keep a decoded stream under the size limit below. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-boot} {dt2-lab-capicola}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
text: What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Trailer: the last 32 bytes of the declared container are an HMAC-SHA256 on the first 16-byte boundary at least 4 bytes past the last section (gap zeroed); it covers everything before it, padding included; the key is derived from material inside the image (a printable string in a decompressed section, found in the bootstrap, plus a fixed constant) - never edit that key material, the device likely verifies with its installed copy. DN1 1.42A is unsigned (trailer all zeros). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Compression: each section is raw or aPLib-variant compressed (not flagged - inferred by whether the bytes depack): LZ77 with interlaced Elias-gamma codes, a biased offset, a last-offset reuse code and a length bonus for far matches, minimum match 2; Elektron's streams keep the furthest match within 1 MiB and the longest at 2,048 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: DN1 vs DN2: bootstrap load address DN2 `0x02000000` / DN1 `0x02000800`; blob (id 7) compressed on DN2, raw on DN1; boot (id 6) absent on DN2, present (raw) on DN1; section 5 (meta) is 15 bytes, stored raw, no destination address, identical size on both; section 8 appears in OS 1.11 compressed (it is the Outbox 8 accessory firmware). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: After patching, recompute: re-encoded section data and its stream length/sum (+ padding to 4 bytes, table length includes the padding), section table offsets/lengths and 16-byte placement (and the count if sections change), the preamble (container size, content checksum), SysEx packet checksums/counters/packet count, and on DN2 the HMAC over everything before the trailer. The page does not say whether the product code, build string or version string must change, nor whether ids must be renumbered. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
text: MIDI DIN runs at 31,250 baud, about 3,125 bytes/s; a 2,209,184-byte image needs at least ~12 minutes (derived, not timed). Do not interrupt. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing}

section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
text: Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem

Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing}

section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem
text: Fixes: prove the link with the stock firmware first; use a dedicated class-compliant USB-MIDI cable for long recovery transfers; disable Windows USB selective suspend and device power management; retry. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

text: CPU fingerprint: NXP MCF5441x (ColdFire V4m with EMAC) - UART8 `0xEC070000`, GPIO `0xEC094000`, eDMA `0xFC044000` (TCDs +0x1000), INTC0-2 `0xFC048000/0xFC04C000/0xFC050000`, DSPI0 `0xFC05C000`, PIT0-3 `0xFC080000-0xFC08C000`, EPORT `0xFC090000`. Stock Ghidra misdecodes EMAC line-A words; digikit uses a separate language spec. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

text: DDR is 128 MiB (DDRMC writes in the bootstrap; earlier 64 MiB claims are wrong): `0x40000000-0x47FFFFFF` cached (ACR0), `0x48000000-0x4FFFFFFF` an uncached alias of the same DDR used for DMA buffers; reset SP `0x48000000`; 32 MiB C++ heap above `0x44000000`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

text: NOR flash 16 MiB, S25FL127S-class (RDID mfg 0x01, id 0x2018); the bootstrap's flash loop uses 512-byte pages and 256 KB erase blocks. The in-OS writer (finding 75) uses 0x100-byte pages and 0x10000 sectors from flash `0x80000` - two code paths, two geometries `[?]`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} {digikit-f75}
